Ran 3 fresh subagents per condition (6 total) against copies of test/fixtures/harness-project. Discarded an entire first batch of 3 condition-A runs after one subject caught, unprompted, that the captured orientation text included a SESSION_INCOMPLETE-gated warning block that the actual fixture could not have produced -- ground-truthed the leak (an unrelated earlier scratch-dir command had left that file behind), re-captured cleanly, and redid all 3 condition-A runs. Documented the discard and its cause in the eval doc rather than hiding it.

Result: 'investigate further', not keep/remove -- all 6 valid runs (3A+3B) independently discovered the same fixture data/reality mismatch (features.json claims passing tests with no corresponding source/test files in git) and converged on identical behavior regardless of condition, so no differential effect of the orientation text was observed. Documented this as a dominant confound specific to this small, self-evidently-inconsistent fixture, not evidence that orientation is worthless in general.

Disclosed a second, smaller deviation: the corrected condition-A batch carried one hint sentence condition B never received (a real, if likely low-impact, departure from 'exactly one intervention'), rather than presenting the comparison as cleaner than it was.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's sed_inplace_targets() recognizes GNU/BSD in-place editing only via a bare `-i`, an attached short-flag suffix (`t.startswith("-i")` on an UNCLUSTERED token, e.g. `-i.bak`), or `--in-place` exactly. Two real, ordinary invocation shapes are missed entirely: (1) CLUSTERED short flags, e.g. `sed -ri 's/a/b/' file` or `sed -ni 's/a/b/' file` (GNU allows combining -r/-n with -i in one token) -- `t.startswith("-i")` is false for `-ri`/`-ni` (the string starts with '-r'/'-n', not '-i'), so the whole in-place-presence guard misses it and sed_inplace_targets() returns [] unconditionally, wrongly ALLOWING an in-place edit of an out-of-scope file; (2) GNU's attached long-form suffix `--in-place=.bak` -- matches neither `t == "--in-place"` (exact match only) nor `t.startswith("-i")` (the token starts with `--`, not `-i`), same wrong-ALLOW outcome. CONFIRMED more reachable in ordinary usage than anything F029 itself fixed (no unusual quoting or '--' needed, just a common flag-combining habit).
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test is the gate -- count omitted here since it drifts on every sibling feature merge; see the header total_features/passing fields for the current count)
features.notes: Discovered by adversarial review of PR #52, round 3 (F029's sed_inplace_targets() separator-index fix). Confirmed pre-existing on main, unrelated to F029's own '--' work -- a different bug class (clustered/long-form flag recognition, not '--' awareness). The existing header comment documents a clustered-flag residual for cp/mv (-rt DIR) only; sed has no equivalent note today, which this feature's fix should also add once landed. Likely fix: recognize any short-flag cluster containing 'i' as specifying in-place mode (mirroring commit-gate.sh's own cluster-scanning approach, F027), and recognize `--in-place=` as an attached-value prefix alongside the exact `--in-place` match. Also noted (round-4 review of PR #52, non-blocking): a pre-existing over-deny, identical on main and unrelated to any F029 change -- `sed -f -i.bak file` denies, since the in-place guard's -e/-f VALUE scan sees the string '-i.bak' and its own startswith('-i') check misfires on it, even though real sed treats '-i.bak' here as -f's script-file VALUE (an unusual but valid filename) and writes nothing. Fails safe (over-deny on an absurd filename), so not urgent, but worth folding into whichever fix lands for this feature's own -ri/--in-place= gaps. Implemented: new IN_PLACE_CLUSTER_PATTERN (`^-[nrEsuz]*i`) recognizes any short-flag cluster ending in "i" where the preceding characters are GNU sed's own argument-less short flags (n, r, E, s, u, z) -- deliberately excludes e/f/l, which take their own argument and consume the rest of the token once encountered (`-fi` is -f's value "i", a file literally named "i", never -f combined with -i, confirmed against real GNU sed). Added alongside the existing exact `--in-place` check: `.startswith("--in-place=")` for the attached long-form suffix. Also folded in the round-4-noted false positive per that review's own suggestion: the two in-place-presence/has_explicit_script any() guards previously scanned ALL pre_separator_args indiscriminately, so a value consumed by a preceding -e/-f (e.g. `sed -f -i.bak file`, where "-i.bak" is a real file used as -f's own script-file argument, confirmed against real GNU sed: prints to stdout, unmodified, no in-place edit at all) was wrongly read as specifying -i. Fixed by computing flag_positions first (mirroring the main loop's own SED_SCRIPT_VALUE_FLAGS skip) and having both guards scan only those positions. Every new shape ground-truthed against real GNU sed (gsed 4.10, installed via Homebrew for this feature since no GNU sed was previously available in this environment) before implementing, not assumed from the ticket description: -ri, -ni, -Ei, -nsi all genuinely enable in-place editing with an empty suffix (since nothing follows "i" in the token); --in-place=.bak genuinely writes a backup with that suffix; -fi and `-f -i.bak file` both genuinely print to stdout with no in-place edit at all. ROUND 1 (adversarial review of PR #65): IN_PLACE_CLUSTER_PATTERN was GNU-only, missing BSD/macOS /usr/bin/sed's own argument-less short flags -- a, H, l (per its own usage string). Confirmed against real /usr/bin/sed (this repo's own stated platform): `sed -ai.bak`/`-Hi.bak`/`-ali.bak` all genuinely in-place edit with a backup, same bug class as the GNU clustered forms, just the BSD half of it left open. Widened to include a/H unconditionally (GNU rejects both outright as invalid options, so it costs nothing there -- a command using them can never reach GNU's own in-place logic regardless of what this hook decides). "l" is a genuine, disclosed flavor conflict: BSD's -l takes no argument (line-buffered output), GNU's -l N takes a MANDATORY numeric one (confirmed: `gsed -li file` prints to stdout, unmodified -- "i" is consumed as -l's value, not a flag). Included "l" anyway, closing the real BSD fail-open at the cost of over-denying an unusual GNU combination (-l clustered with -i in one token, an uncommon habit itself) -- accepted, same class as this hook's other documented safe-direction residuals. Also closed a mutation gap: the e/f exclusion (the single most-argued claim in the pattern's own comment) had zero coverage -- a single trailing argument after `-fi` isn't enough to discriminate (a wrongly-triggered guard still swallows the lone token as a fake implicit script and finds zero targets either way, landing on the same ALLOW by coincidence); needed TWO trailing arguments so a wrongly-triggered guard consumes the first as the fake script and then wrongly finds the second as a real target. Added a 3-flag cluster test and a quoted-cluster test, both previously correct but unpinned. Disclosed, not fixed (reviewer's own framing, would not block): GNU's own unambiguous long-option ABBREVIATION of --in-place (--i, --in, --in-p, ..., confirmed all perform real in-place edits) is not recognized, matching only the exact string or the `--in-place=` prefix -- pre-existing on main before this feature touched the guard at all, lower reachability than the clustered-short-flag gaps this feature closes, and would need the same unambiguous-prefix-resolution machinery F032 built for commit-gate.sh's own long flags to close properly -- a candidate for its own future feature, not folded in here.
approaches_tried: Installed GNU sed via Homebrew (gsed 4.10) specifically to ground-truth every claim in this feature against real execution rather than reasoning from memory, since this environment had no GNU sed available (a standing limitation another reviewer flagged earlier this session for a different feature). Mutation-tested two ways: reverting the clustered/long-form recognition to the old exact/prefix-only check fails exactly the 6 new clustered/long-form assertions; reverting flag_positions to include every position (undoing the round-4 fold-in) fails exactly the new 'sed -f -i.bak file' no-deny assertion.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's ANSI_C_ESCAPE_PATTERN (F033) decodes \xHH and \nnn escapes inside a $'...' span but does not recognize \cX (control-char, e.g. \cA -> 0x01), \uHHHH (4-hex-digit Unicode codepoint), or \UHHHHHHHH (8-hex-digit Unicode codepoint) -- all three are real bash $'...' escape forms. A traversal segment spelled via one of these (e.g. \u002e\u002e for '..') would be left as literal, undecoded text by the current decoder (since it's treated as an 'unrecognized escape', matching the same 'leave backslash+char literal' fallback used for genuinely unknown escapes), so normalize() never sees a real '..' to resolve, while real bash WOULD decode it and genuinely escape scope -- the exact same vulnerability class as F033, just a narrower/rarer set of escape spellings. VERIFIED against this repo's actual bash (3.2.57): \u002e and \U0000002e are NOT decoded at all here (both left as literal backslash-plus-text, e.g. `$'a\u002eb'` prints literally `a\u002eb`) -- so \u/\U are not a live concern in THIS environment's bash version specifically, though the gap in this hook's own decoder remains real for any bash new enough to support them (believed added around bash 4.2, per documentation; UNVERIFIED in this environment, since no bash newer than 3.2.57 was available to test against directly -- found by adversarial review of PR #57). \cX (control-char) IS decoded by this bash (`$'a\cAb'` -> 0x01), but \cX escapes only ever produce non-printable control bytes (0x00-0x1F), which can never spell '.' (0x2e) or '/' (0x2f) -- so \cX's own gap in this hook's decoder, while real, is NOT independently traversal-exploitable the way \u/\U could be on a newer bash. Net: on THIS repo's bash, none of \c/\u/\U currently reaches a live bypass; the residual is worth closing for portability (a newer bash elsewhere) and completeness, not because it's exploitable here today.
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test is the gate -- count omitted here since it drifts on every sibling feature merge; see the header total_features/passing fields for the current count)
features.notes: Discovered while implementing F033 (same feature, deliberately scoped out to keep that fix narrow and match the description's own confirmed exploit shapes). Likely fix: extend ANSI_C_ESCAPE_PATTERN with \c., \u{4 hex}, \U{8 hex} alternatives and their decode logic in _decode_ansi_c_escape(), verifying each against whatever bash version is available first (this repo's bash 3.2.57 may predate \u/\U support, added in a later bash version -- confirm before assuming the vulnerability is live here). Implemented: ANSI_C_ESCAPE_PATTERN extended with c(.), u([0-9A-Fa-f]{1,4}), and U([0-9A-Fa-f]{1,8}) alternatives; _decode_ansi_c_escape() decodes \cX via ord(X.upper()) & 0x1F (bash's real formula -- verified empirically across 10 characters spanning letters/digits/punctuation; a naive XOR-0x40 convention some documentation implies gives the WRONG byte below 0x40, e.g. \c? [SUPERSEDED, see ROUND 2 below: this specific character has a genuine bash-version split] really decodes to 0x1F, not the 0x7F XOR would produce) and \u/\U via chr(int(hexdigits, 16)), matching \x's own greedy up-to-N-digit consumption (verified: \u2b consumes BOTH hex-looking chars as one 2-digit codepoint 0x2B, not \u2 plus literal 'b'). ELEVATED FROM THE ORIGINAL TICKET'S OWN RISK ASSESSMENT: the ticket called \u/\U 'believed added around bash 4.2, UNVERIFIED in this environment, since no bash newer than 3.2.57 was available.' Installed bash 5.3.15 via Homebrew specifically to check directly rather than leave that unverified -- confirmed \u002e and \U0000002e BOTH genuinely decode to '.' on 5.3.15, meaning this is a LIVE bypass on any sufficiently new bash, not merely a theoretical portability gap. A \U value exceeding Unicode's own max codepoint (0x10FFFF) is a documented, disclosed residual left undecoded (real bash uses an extended, pre-RFC-3629 UTF-8 byte encoding for these that Python's chr() cannot represent -- confirmed real bash still produces SOME byte sequence for \U11000000 and a raw surrogate \U0000D800, but neither can ever spell '.' or '/' regardless of exact byte representation, so replicating bash's own extended encoding was judged not worth the complexity). [SUPERSEDED, see ROUND 2 below: this claim was wrong and a round-2 reviewer proved it] Testing limitation, disclosed: \cX's exact byte-value correctness (the & 0x1F formula, as opposed to some other wrong formula) cannot be observed via this hook's ALLOW/DENY interface at all, in principle -- a control byte's exact value never changes whether the resulting path matches a scope prefix, so no hook-level test can discriminate correct from incorrect \cX decoding; verified instead via direct Python-level testing during implementation (10 characters against real bash 5.3.15), not via test/run-tests.sh. ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #66, post-merge): found a NEW, genuine fail-open this feature itself introduced, more severe than the bug it fixed. _decode_ansi_c_escape()'s \u/\U handling only guarded a codepoint above Unicode's own max (0x10FFFF, via a try/except around chr()) but let a LONE SURROGATE (0xD800-0xDFFF) through unchecked -- Python's chr() constructs a string containing one WITHOUT raising. This hook's own LATER json.dumps()/print() of the denial message DOES raise (UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed) once a resolved path contains one, and since this hook is fail-OPEN on any exception, a PLAIN out-of-scope write with NO traversal at all -- just a lone surrogate escape anywhere in the target -- silently bypassed detection entirely (confirmed by direct execution: rc 0, no deny fields, traceback on stderr only, write genuinely lands). Composed with the pre-existing F031/F033 defenses too: a real '..' traversal plus a trailing lone surrogate ALSO crashed past the point where the real target had already been correctly resolved. Fixed with a shared _unicode_escape_or_literal() helper used by both \u and \U, rejecting both the surrogate range and the out-of-range case into the literal-text fallback. Also found the \c? claim was wrong for bash 5.3.15 specifically (this repo's own prior verification against 5.3.15 was flatly contradicted by a direct re-measurement: 5.3.15 decodes \c? to 0x7F/DEL via a special case, not 0x1F -- confirmed both versions directly): bash 3.2.57 uses the general AND-0x1F formula for '?' but 5.3.15 special-cases it to DEL. This is a genuine, disclosed version split with no security implication either way (neither 0x1F nor 0x7F is '.' or '/'); matched modern bash's special case since that's more likely to be encountered broadly. Also closed a testing-methodology error: an earlier round claimed \cX's exact formula correctness could never be observed via this hook's ALLOW/DENY interface -- proven false: the JSON-encoded denial message renders a control byte as a distinct \u00XX escape sequence, fully inspectable via assert_contains; added \c0 (pins the general formula) and \c? (pins the version-specific special case) tests using exactly this technique, both mutation-tested. Corrected a stale comment in unquote_token() that still claimed \cX/\u/\U were not decoded.
approaches_tried: Installed bash 5.3.15 via Homebrew alongside the existing bash 3.2.57 specifically to ground-truth \u/\U against a version new enough to support them, since the original ticket left this unverified. Also hit and worked around a tooling artifact: typing the literal 4 characters \u followed by 4 hex digits directly in a Bash-tool command string or even a Write-tool content parameter silently collapsed to the single decoded Unicode character (apparently JSON/Python-string unicode-escape interpretation somewhere upstream of the shell) -- confirmed this was happening even via Write by checking the file's actual bytes afterward. Worked around by constructing the literal backslash character via chr(92) concatenation in a Python script and writing the file directly from Python, verified byte-for-byte via repr() before trusting it, for every place this session needed to embed a literal \u/\U escape sequence (both the ground-truth probes and the final test/run-tests.sh edit). Mutation-tested: reverting the pattern and decoder to their F033-era (no c/u/U) state fails exactly the 2 new \u/\U traversal assertions -- the \c and ordinary-\u-character tests do NOT fail under this same reversion (both still ALLOW either way, since neither decoded nor literal form changes whether the path still starts with 'src/parser/'), which is expected and consistent with F033's own documented precedent for its 'unrecognized escape' test -- those two tests pin non-regression, not decode-correctness, which was instead verified directly via the Python decoder function.

Round 2: this PR was merged directly on Ovidiu's explicit instruction before the adversarial review had reported back; the review then found a genuine, severe fail-open regression already live on main. Fixed immediately: verified the crash myself by direct execution before touching code (confirmed rc 0, no deny fields, UnicodeEncodeError on stderr, matching the review's exact reproduction), then implemented and mutation-tested all three fixes (surrogate/out-of-range guard shared between \u and \U; the \c? modern-bash special case; corrected the stale unquote_token() comment). Mutation-tested: reverting the surrogate guard to the old unguarded try/except fails exactly the 6 new surrogate-regression assertions; reverting the \c? special case fails exactly its own 1 new assertion; reverting the general AND-0x1F formula (to XOR-0x40) fails exactly the \c0 assertion.

Round 3 (adversarial review of PR #67, round 2): found the SAME crash-to-silent-ALLOW class had recurred one branch over, in \cX itself, already live on main via the ORIGINAL PR #66 merge (no surrogate needed at all -- ANSI_C_ESCAPE_PATTERN's c(.) captures any single character, and 102 distinct Unicode characters uppercase to TWO characters via Python's str.upper(), crashing ord() with TypeError). Confirmed live via direct execution before fixing (an unrelated \c<that character> anywhere in a compound command silently allowed an ordinarily-denied plain-ASCII out-of-scope write elsewhere in the SAME command). Fixed by falling back to the original (non-uppercased) character when upper() returns more than one character, before the & 0x1F mask -- diverges from real bash's own byte-wise result for these characters, but \cX can never spell '.' or '/' on either reading. Also closed a genuine, previously-uncovered test gap: _unicode_escape_or_literal()'s out-of-range (>0x10FFFF) half had zero coverage of its own (only the surrogate half was mutation-tested in round 2) -- dropping just that half of the guard's condition still passed the full suite while crashing the hook live. Added a dedicated test for it. Both fixes mutation-tested: reverting the \cX fallback fails exactly its 2 new assertions; dropping the out-of-range half of the guard fails exactly its own 2 new assertions. Marked two now-superseded claims in this feature's own round-1 notes ('\c? decodes to 0x1F' as a universal truth; '\cX correctness is unobservable in principle') rather than leaving them stated as unqualified fact alongside their later correction, per this repo's own precedent against self-contradictory records (commit 4e3f23c). The reviewer's broader systemic-hardening suggestion (make the per-target analysis total: on ANY decoder exception, fall back to checking the raw undecoded token rather than aborting the whole scan, rather than reactively patching each specific exception type as found) was NOT implemented here -- filed as F042 instead, since it is a genuine architectural improvement distinct from closing the two specific, now-fixed bugs, and deserves its own dedicated implementation and review cycle rather than being bolted onto an already-multi-round emergency fix. The reviewer's own framing: this narrow fix is 'complete for the branch it targets' (the whole \u/\U/\c codepoint space was checked), so nothing is currently known-broken; F042 is defense-in-depth against the NEXT unknown exception type in this same decoder, not a currently-open bypass.

features.description: skills/harness-init/commit-gate.sh.template's own unquote_token() strips a $'...' ANSI-C-quote wrapper with a plain `re.sub(r"\$'((?:[^'\\]|\\.)*)'", r"\1", token)` and never decodes escapes inside it, and never strips a bare interior backslash either -- unlike enforce-scope.sh's own unquote_token(), which F038 already hardened to run every $'...' span's contents through ANSI_C_ESCAPE_PATTERN/_decode_ansi_c_escape(). Because is_git_token() (the ONLY thing that decides whether a segment is git-shaped at all) is fed these under-decoded tokens, any escaped spelling of "git" makes segment_subcommand() return (None, None), which skips this hook's ENTIRE analysis for that segment -- BOTH the compound-stage-and-commit check AND the secret-scan check, not just one. CONFIRMED live (rc=0, completely empty output, silently ALLOWED) for `g\it commit -a -m "test"`, `\g\i\t commit -a -m "test"`, and `$'\x67it' commit -a -m "test"`, each against a control (`git commit -a -m "test"`) that correctly denies compound-stage-and-commit. Also confirmed the SECRET-SCAN bypass specifically: with a real secret-shaped line staged, `git commit -m "add config"` correctly denies (secret-assignment), but `g\it commit -m "add config"` silently allows the exact same staged secret through. `\"git\"` (backslash before a quote character) is a confirmed benign exception -- it produces the literal word `"git"`, which real bash reports as command-not-found, not a bypass. This is the same severity class as F025 (a full, silent gate no-op), reachable via ordinary backslash-escaping (`\git` is a common shell-alias-bypass idiom, not an adversarial contortion), and higher priority than F045 was, since F045's own gap turned out not to exist while this one is proven live and end-to-end.
features.coverage: n/a (shell suite, no coverage tooling; full_test is the gate -- count omitted here since it drifts on every sibling feature merge; see the header total_features/passing fields for the current count)
features.notes:
Discovered by adversarial review of PR #77 (F045), while confirming F045's own "not a bug" conclusion about is_git_token()'s quoted-name handling -- the reviewer went further and tried escaped forms, finding a much more severe, live, full-gate bypass in the surrounding unquote_token()/segment_subcommand() machinery that F045's own narrow scope didn't cover. Independently reproduced by the lead (not just the reviewer) before filing: both the compound-stage-and-commit bypass and the secret-scan bypass confirmed live against fresh fixtures. Suggested fix is TWO DISTINCT ports, not one plus a check (round-2 review of PR #77 caught that the first framing understated the second half): (1) ANSI_C_ESCAPE_PATTERN/_decode_ansi_c_escape() from enforce-scope.sh.template's own unquote_token() (F038), decoding escapes INSIDE a $'...' span, and (2) enforce-scope.sh.template's own FINAL unquote_token() line, `return re.sub(r"\\(.)", r"\1", token)` (F031), which strips a bare interior backslash OUTSIDE quotes too. Verified by simulating both ports against the 3 confirmed bypasses: the F038 port ALONE fixes only `$'\x67it'` (the ANSI-C-quoted case) -- `g\it` and `\g\i\t` (the two MORE common, everyday-alias-bypass spellings) need the F031 port specifically. Shipping only the F038 port would be a half-fix that still lets the more common spellings through. Given severity (a proven secret-scan bypass), recommend picking this up immediately after F045 merges, ahead of the lower-severity F046-F050 items already queued, despite this feature's own numeric ID sorting after them.

FIXED: ported both pieces, confirmed independently necessary via mutation testing (matching the reviewer's own prediction exactly): ANSI_C_ESCAPE_PATTERN/_decode_ansi_c_escape()/_unicode_escape_or_literal() (F038) decode escapes inside a $'...' span; the final `return re.sub(r"\\(.)", r"\1", token)` line (F031) strips a bare interior backslash outside quotes. Re-verified all 3 confirmed bypasses now deny (compound-stage-and-commit), the secret-scan bypass specifically is closed (a real staged secret is caught through the escaped form the same as the bare form), and the one benign exception (`\"git\"`, backslash-before-a-quote, real bash reports command-not-found) is correctly NOT misread as a violation. Ran the full existing 1161-assertion suite before adding new tests to confirm zero regressions from the port. Added 16 new assertions (4 assert_contains, 4 assert_deny_json, 2 assert_not_contains, 6 assert_rc0). Mutation-tested twice: full revert -> exactly 8 failures (the 2 discriminating assertions -- deny_json and contains -- for each of the 4 bypass-shape tests; rc0 trivially passes either way since both ALLOW and DENY exit 0); removing only the F031 backslash-strip line (keeping F038's ANSI-C decode) -> exactly 6 failures, and specifically NOT the ANSI-C test, confirming the reviewer's own prediction that the F038 port alone only closes the ANSI-C-quoted spelling, not the two backslash-escaped ones.

ROUND 2 (review of PR #79): the round-1 fix above (ANSI-C decode + blanket backslash-strip in unquote_token()) closed the escaped-"git" bypass but introduced a new one: has_staging_flag()'s "--" pathspec-separator check and its long-flag/short-flag-cluster bare-value skip both key off the fully backslash-stripped token, so a real bash `'\--'` (a literal 3-char pathspec, never the actual "--" separator -- confirmed against real git) collapsed to plain "--" and wrongly ended the flag scan before reaching a real -i/-a placed after it. Independently reproduced end-to-end for the single-quoted, double-quoted, and ANSI-C ($'\\--') forms. Fixed by adding _flag_view() (a second, non-backslash-stripping per-token view, mirroring enforce-scope.sh's own established pattern) and _consumes_next_token(), threading a parallel `views` list through parse_command() -> check_compound_stage_and_commit() -> has_staging_flag(tokens, views); the "--" check and value-skip use the view, while flag-MATCH checks keep using the fully-unquoted token (over-recognition there is safe-directional). First attempt at this fix was itself broken (computed the view from the already-stripped token, a no-op) and separately surfaced an unrelated regression: main()'s early short-circuit still unpacked parse_command()'s tuples as 3-tuples after the views field was added, silently disabling the whole gate (an uncaught ValueError under this hook's fail-open exception handling) -- both caught and fixed before verifying the round-2 fix itself. Also ground-truthed (against real git) and closed a false claim my own fix's comment made about segment_subcommand()'s GIT_FLAGS_WITH_VALUE/"-"-prefix skips being converted too -- they weren't, and confirmed that gap is not independently reachable (any divergent token there makes real git reject the whole invocation before committing, since it sits before the subcommand rather than after it). Added 14 new assertions (4 assert_contains, 4 assert_deny_json, 5 assert_rc0, 1 assert_not_contains). Ran the full 1191-assertion suite (1177 prior + 14 new) with zero regressions. Mutation-tested by reverting to the pre-round-2 commit_gate.sh.template: exactly 6 failures (the 2 discriminating assertions for each of the 3 escape-form denial tests), with the control case and the real-"--" no-false-positive case correctly unaffected, confirming the new tests discriminate precisely this fix.

Round-2 review (APPROVE) caught two accounting errors in the notes above, both confirmed and corrected: the round-1 "16 new assertions" parenthetical summed to 19, not 16 (fixed to list actual assert_* call counts); the round-2 "8 new / 1183 prior" was wrong on both numbers (actual: 14 new, 1177 prior, 1177+14=1191 -- verified by diffing assert_* call counts between this branch and the pre-round-2 commit). Reviewer also independently re-verified every claim end-to-end against the real hook/bash/git (not an extracted module), re-fuzzed unquote_token()/_flag_view() over ~2600 escape inputs with 0 exceptions, and found a separate pre-existing gap (not introduced by this PR, confirmed identical on main): `git commit -m x tracked.txt` / `git commit -m x -- tracked.txt` commits a pathspec's working-tree content directly, bypassing the index entirely, so the secret scan (which reads `git diff --cached`) never sees it. Filed separately as F052 rather than expanding this feature's scope.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's target-extraction pipeline does not truncate a token at an embedded NUL byte the way real bash truncates a word at its first NUL when building argv. CONFIRMED: `echo x > $'src/other/bad.txt\x00/../../parser/ok.txt'` -- real bash decodes \x00 to a genuine NUL byte and truncates the argument there, so the real write target is 'src/other/bad.txt' (OUT of scope), but this hook's normalize()/scope-check pipeline processes the WHOLE string (NUL and all), resolving the '..' segments after the NUL and landing on 'src/parser/ok.txt' (IN scope) -- wrongly ALLOWED. CONFIRMED as pre-existing on origin/main BEFORE F033 too (not a regression from F033's own fix); F033 makes this specific route more direct since \x00 now genuinely decodes to a real NUL byte inside a $'...' span, where previously the literal 4-character string '\x00' just stayed as inert text. Likely fix: truncate the token at the first NUL character (if any) immediately after unquote_token() finishes decoding, before normalize() or the scope-prefix comparison ever see it.

features.notes: Discovered by adversarial review of PR #57 (F033), explicitly confirmed as a pre-existing bypass unchanged by that PR (verified ALLOW on both origin/main before F033 and the F033 branch) -- filed alongside F038 per the reviewer's own recommendation, same general vulnerability class (a shell-level string transformation this hook's pipeline doesn't replicate before the scope check runs). Implemented exactly as the ticket's own likely-fix suggested: write_targets()'s final list comprehension now truncates each unquote_token()-decoded target at its first embedded NUL (`.split("\0", 1)[0]`), applied AFTER decoding completes and BEFORE normalize()/the scope-prefix comparison ever see it -- this single choke point covers every decode route that could produce an embedded NUL (F031's backslash-unescape, F033's \x/\nnn, F038's \c/\u/\U), not just the \x00 spelling the ticket's own reproduction used. Verified the octal \000 spelling produces the identical bypass through a DIFFERENT decode path (ANSI_C_ESCAPE_PATTERN's octal group) before fixing, confirming the single-choke-point fix genuinely covers both, not just the one form tested. ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #68): found two issues, both fixed. (1) A genuine, previously-invisible bug in this PR's OWN commit: the docstring comment listing NUL escape spellings (\x00/\000/\c@/...) had a literal 0x00 byte where the text \U00000000 was meant -- confirmed via a raw byte scan (git's own binary-file heuristic only samples the first 8000 bytes of a file, so this NUL at offset ~61311 never showed up as a binary-file warning or rendered oddly in the diff). Confirmed the real impact directly: `grep -q 'def write_targets' <template>` returned rc=1/no-match on the byte-exact file (Claude Code's own bundled ugrep runs with -I, treating any NUL-containing file as binary and silently skipping it) -- the exact 'an empty result is not a negative result' trap this repo's own global CLAUDE.md environment notes already warn about, now demonstrated against this repo's own most-reviewed file. Fixed by replacing the byte with the intended literal text. Added a permanent regression guard: the existing per-template bash-syntax-check loop in test/run-tests.sh now also scans each template's raw bytes for an embedded NUL (a shell/grep-based check can't reliably search FOR a NUL -- a NUL in a shell argument truncates the argument to empty, which then matches everything, confirmed empirically while writing this check -- so it reads the file directly in Python instead). Mutation-tested: reinserting a stray NUL byte into a throwaway copy of the template is caught by exactly this new assertion. (2) The two original NUL-truncation tests both happened to place the NUL immediately before a '/', so a narrower, WRONG fix (truncating only at a NUL-then-slash pair, not any NUL) would have passed both -- confirmed against real bash that a NUL followed by a non-slash character (e.g. '\x00x') still genuinely truncates the same way. Added a third test with the NUL not adjacent to a slash; mutation-tested (the narrower truncate-at-NUL-slash mutant now fails exactly this new test's 2 assertions, confirming it's the discriminating one the first two tests were missing). ROUND 3 (adversarial review of PR #68, round 2, optional follow-up): the round-2 NUL-byte guard only covered the *.sh.template loop (6 files copied per-project); hooks/*.sh (the 3 files that ship DIRECTLY with the plugin to every user, not copied per-project) were silently uncovered -- confirmed by inserting a NUL into a throwaway copy of session-start.sh and observing zero guard-related failures beforehand. Extended the same NUL-byte scan to the existing hooks/*.sh bash-syntax-check loop. Mutation-tested by reinserting a NUL into a throwaway copy of session-start.sh: the new assertion correctly fails (among a larger cascade of collateral failures from that specific mutation's placement corrupting the shebang line, which is a property of where the mutation was inserted for testing convenience, not a gap in the guard itself).
approaches_tried: Ground-truthed the exact reproduction against real bash before implementing: `echo x > $'src/other/bad.txt\x00/../../parser/ok.txt'` genuinely creates a file named exactly "src/other/bad.txt" (confirmed via `ls`), not the untruncated string. Confirmed the hook wrongly ALLOWed this exact command before the fix (rc 0, empty stdout), and correctly denies naming the real truncated target after. Mutation-tested: reverting the `.split("\0", 1)[0]` truncation fails exactly its 4 new assertions (both the \x00 and octal \000 traversal cases), nothing else.

Round 2 fixes (adversarial review of PR #68): fixed a stray literal NUL byte the original commit accidentally introduced into the template source itself (found via a raw byte scan, not visible in git diff); added a permanent per-template NUL-byte scan to test/run-tests.sh's existing syntax-check loop to catch any recurrence, mutation-tested by reinserting a NUL into a throwaway copy; added a discriminating NUL-not-adjacent-to-a-slash test, mutation-tested against the specific narrower-and-wrong fix the reviewer identified as passing the original two tests.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's write_targets() compares the COMMAND NAME token (command_tokens[0]) RAW against ("cp","mv")/("tee","rm")/"sed", so quoting or backslash-escaping the command name itself evades recognition entirely, not just its flags or targets. CONFIRMED: `\rm src/other/f.txt`, `"rm" src/other/f.txt`, and `'rm' src/other/f.txt` are ALL wrongly ALLOWED (no target extracted at all, since the raw token is '\\rm'/'"rm"'/"'rm'", none of which equals the bare string "rm"), even though `\rm` (backslash-prefixed) is a common, everyday idiom for bypassing a shell alias named rm/cp/mv, not an adversarial evasion technique. Arguably a WIDER hole than F035 itself, since it defeats every command-type extractor (cp_mv_targets(), all_flagless_tokens() for tee/rm, sed_inplace_targets()) in one step, before any of their own (now-fixed) flag/target recognition logic even runs. Likely fix: compare _flag_view(command_tokens[0]) instead of the raw token, mirroring the same pattern used throughout F035 -- this is a command-name recognition check, not a target-value extraction, so no double-unquote risk applies (the command name itself is never returned as a target).

features.notes:
Discovered by adversarial review of PR #59 (F035), during a systematic sweep for the same 'raw comparison evadable by quoting' bug class this feature's own fix addresses elsewhere in the same file. Confirmed identical on main and the F035 branch (pre-existing, not a regression). Verified directly: `\\rm src/other/f.txt` and `"rm" src/other/f.txt` both exit rc 0 with no permissionDecision field at all against a fixture scoped to src/parser/, i.e. a genuine silent bypass, not merely a misnamed denial.

FIXED: confirmed the bypass live against a src/parser/-scoped fixture before touching code (\rm, "rm", 'rm', \cp, and "sed" -i all exited rc=0 with no permissionDecision field at all). Fixed both call sites that had the raw-comparison bug: write_targets()'s own cp/mv/tee/rm dispatch (introduced a `command_name = _flag_view(command_tokens[0])` local and compared that instead of the raw token), and sed_inplace_targets()'s own internal `tokens[0] != "sed"` guard (compared _flag_view(tokens[0]) instead) -- the ticket's own suggested fix named only the write_targets() dispatch, but inspecting sed_inplace_targets() directly (it's called unconditionally from write_targets()'s else branch for any non-cp/mv/tee/rm command) showed the identical bug at its own internal command-name check, a second site the ticket didn't call out. No double-unquote risk: _flag_view() is used here purely for command-NAME recognition, never as a returned target value, matching the established F035 convention. Re-verified live post-fix: all five bypass spellings now correctly deny with the real target named, and an in-scope backslash-escaped rm still allows (no false positive).
approaches_tried: Ground-truthed the bypass via direct hook execution against a throwaway fixture (src/parser/ scope) before writing any fix, per session discipline: confirmed rc=0/no-decision for \rm, "rm", 'rm', \cp, and "sed" -i, and rc=0/deny for the unescaped control case, isolating the bug to the raw command-name comparison. Fixed both call sites (write_targets()'s dispatch and sed_inplace_targets()'s own guard) using the existing _flag_view() helper, matching the F035 pattern. Added 6 new regression tests (5 bypass-now-denies cases across rm/cp/sed, plus 1 in-scope no-false-positive case) to test/run-tests.sh. Mutation-tested by reverting the template fix in a working copy via `git stash push -- <file>` while keeping the new tests: confirmed exactly the 10 expected new assertions failed (2 per bypass case: JSON-deny-form and real-target-name) and nothing else regressed, then restored the fix and reconfirmed 1028/1028 green.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's sed_inplace_targets() in-place-presence guard recognizes only the exact string "--in-place" or the attached "--in-place=" prefix -- it does not resolve GNU's own unambiguous long-option ABBREVIATION feature. CONFIRMED against real GNU sed (gsed 4.10): --i, --in, --in-p, --in-pla, --in-plac, and --i=.bak all genuinely perform a real in-place edit (with the given suffix where one is attached), since --in-place is the only GNU sed long option starting with "--i" (no ambiguity to resolve against). Each of these is wrongly ALLOWED today. Pre-existing on main before F037 touched this guard at all; lower reachability than F037's clustered-short-flag gaps (an abbreviated long flag is a less common habit than combining short flags), and closing it properly needs the same unambiguous-prefix-resolution machinery F032 built for commit-gate.sh's own long flags (GIT_COMMIT_LONG_OPTIONS / _resolve_long_flag()) -- a full GNU sed long-option universe would need to be mechanically extracted the same way, not assembled from memory.

features.notes:
Discovered by adversarial review of PR #65, round 1 (F037's clustered -i / --in-place= fix). Confirmed pre-existing on main, unrelated to F037's own changes -- a different bug class (long-option abbreviation, not clustered-short-flag or attached-long-form recognition). Reviewer's own framing: "would not block" F037 on this, lower reachability, candidate for its own future feature.

FIXED: mechanically extracted GNU sed's full long-option universe from `gsed --help` (GNU sed 4.10, installed via `brew install gnu-sed` for F037), built SED_LONG_OPTIONS + _resolve_sed_long_flag()/_sed_long_flag_name() mirroring commit-gate.sh's F032 pattern (GIT_COMMIT_LONG_OPTIONS/_resolve_long_flag()). The in-place-presence guard now recognizes any unambiguous abbreviation of --in-place, bare or with an attached =SUFFIX (confirmed against real gsed: --i, --in-p, --i=.bak all genuinely in-place edit). SCOPE NARROWED from the ticket's own note during implementation: has_explicit_script's --expression=/--file= recognition is extended ONLY for the ATTACHED abbreviated form (--exp=script), not a bare one (--exp script) -- proved via mutation testing that the bare form is a safe, self-cancelling residual (the walking loop's own unrelated 1-token-too-few skip for an unrecognized bare flag exactly cancels against has_explicit_script's own one-token misclassification, for a SINGLE bare abbreviated script flag), while fixing has_explicit_script's bare-form recognition WITHOUT also reworking the walking loop's token-consumption count would have broken that symmetry and named the wrong (script-fragment) string in the denial reason. Confirmed live: the bare-form command still correctly denies (mutation-tested: reverting the whole fix does NOT change this case's outcome, only the attached form's). [SUPERSEDED, see ROUND 2 below -- this cancellation argument is FALSE whenever the flag's value is not a flagless token (starts with "-", or is exactly "--"); it does not generalize, and was disproven by adversarial review with a live, real-gsed-confirmed fail-open.]

ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #71): the ABOVE scope-narrowing reasoning was WRONG, not merely under-tested -- it is a real, live fail-open, not just a mis-naming edge case. Reviewer constructed and confirmed against real gsed 4.10: `sed -i --fi -x.sed <out-of-scope>` and `sed -i --fi -- <out-of-scope>` (with a file literally named "--" holding a script) both genuinely in-place edit, and the hook (round-1 code) silently ALLOWED both -- reachable even against round 1's OWN newly-recognized --in-place, since `sed --in-place --fi -x.sed <out-of-scope>` hits the identical gap one flag later. The cancellation argument's unstated precondition: it only holds when the flag's value is itself a flagless token, so the (round-1, unfixed) walking loop's `view.startswith("-"): i += 1` branch never fires on it. A value that looks like a flag (leading "-", or exactly "--") breaks that precondition, and the two 'off by one' errors stop cancelling and start compounding -- the REAL target gets swallowed as the implicit script instead, not just mis-named. FIXED by building _sed_consumes_next_as_script() (bare or attached, exact or abbreviated) as ONE shared predicate used identically at all four sites that need to agree on 'does this flag consume 2 tokens or 1': _separator_index(), the flag_positions walk, has_explicit_script, and the main token-walking loop. Reviewer's own mutation testing (independently reproduced): all four fail-open shapes now DENY and name the real file (confirmed with a fresh mutation-test round: reverting round 2's fix reintroduces exactly 8 failures across exactly these cases, nothing else). Bonus: the symmetric fix also corrects a genuine PRE-EXISTING false positive (`sed --fi -i.bak file1 file2` was wrongly DENIED -- the unrecognized `--fi` left "-i.bak" looking like a flag position that IN_PLACE_CLUSTER_PATTERN then mismatched as enabling in-place mode, even though real gsed treats "-i.bak" as --file's own script-file value and performs no in-place edit at all -- the same class PR #52 round 4 already fixed for the exact-spelling form, reintroduced via abbreviation). Reviewer also found the identical abbreviation-comparison gap in cp_mv_targets()'s own TARGET_DIRECTORY_FLAGS (a different function, out of F041's scope) -- filed separately as F048 per the reviewer's own recommendation, not folded into this fix.

ROUND 3 (fresh independent review after the round-2 reviewer stalled on repeated transient API infrastructure errors): the round-2 fix itself held up against an independent differential fuzzing sweep (406,900+ modelled command sequences vs. a from-scratch GNU-sed-parsing model, cross-validated against 1,600 real gsed executions) -- zero new fail-opens, zero new over-denies relative to round 2. The one finding was a TEST-COVERAGE gap, not a code defect: per-site mutation testing showed _separator_index() -- one of the four sites sharing _sed_consumes_next_as_script() -- had no test discriminating it on its own, even though the aggregate revert-the-whole-fix test correctly showed 8 failures. Confirmed live: `sed --fi -- -i <out-of-scope>` (in-place flag AFTER a value-consumed '--', via a file literally named '--' holding a script) genuinely in-place edits in real gsed, and reverting ONLY _separator_index() flips this hook's verdict to a silent ALLOW while every other test still passes -- the existing f041r test doesn't discriminate this because its -i appears BEFORE --fi, so an unfixed separator index there doesn't drop the in-place flag. Added f041w pinning this specific site. Also fixed a cosmetic inaccuracy in the SED_LONG_OPTIONS comment (paraphrased vs. the real gsed error text) flagged by the same review. A separate, genuinely different and pre-existing bug class was found and filed as F049 (the -i backup-SUFFIX value itself is an unchecked second write target via GNU sed's '*' expansion -- present on main too, not introduced by this fix, not folded into this PR per the reviewer's own recommendation).
approaches_tried: Ground-truthed GNU sed's full long-option universe via `gsed --help` output (mechanical extraction, not memory), then ground-truthed 8 abbreviation spellings against real gsed (bare and attached, for both --in-place and --expression) before writing any fix. First implementation attempt symmetrically fixed BOTH bare and attached abbreviation recognition across all 3 sed_inplace_targets() call sites (the in-place guard, has_explicit_script, and the main token-walking loop's 2-token skip, plus _separator_index()) via a shared _sed_bare_script_value_flag() helper. Mutation testing this first attempt (git stash of the template fix) found the bare-abbreviated-form test case did NOT discriminate old vs new code at all -- traced this to a genuine structural self-cancellation (proved algebraically: an unrecognized bare flag's 1-token-too-few skip in old code is exactly offset by has_explicit_script's own 1-token misclassification of the next token as an implicit script, landing on the identical real target either way, for a single bare abbreviated flag). Concluded the bare-form walking-loop fix added complexity without closing an actual bypass, and scaled the fix back to ONLY the in-place guard (bare+attached) and has_explicit_script's ATTACHED form -- re-verified via a second mutation-test round that exactly the 4 discriminating cases (2 assertions each) fail on revert, full suite 1047/1047 green.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's _decode_ansi_c_escape() (and by extension unquote_token()'s whole $'...' decoding pass) is reactively hardened against specific exception types as they're found (F038 round 2: a lone-surrogate ValueError-that-isn't; F038 round 3: a multi-char-uppercase TypeError) rather than being structurally total. This hook's own design is fail-OPEN on any exception (an empty DENY_REASON means deny_json() never runs), which the header documents as covering environment failures (unresolvable project root, unreadable scope file, unparseable JSON) -- but an exception raised INSIDE the per-target analysis by attacker-shaped input is a different thing: it is an input-controlled lever that silently disables enforcement for the WHOLE command, not just the one problematic target. Two distinct exception types (ValueError-turned-ValueError-that-isn't via chr() on a surrogate, and TypeError via ord() on a multi-char string) have now been found and fixed individually in the SAME function; there is no reason to believe these are the last two. Proposed fix (per the reviewer who raised this, not yet implemented or verified): make the per-target scan structurally total by wrapping the decode/normalize step for EACH target individually, so a decoder exception on ONE target falls back to checking that target's RAW, undecoded text against scope instead of aborting the entire scan (preserving the fail-open contract for genuine environment failures, which happen before any per-target loop even starts, while removing 'crash the decoder on target N => skip every target in the command, including targets 1 through N-1 and N+1 onward').

features.notes:
Discovered by adversarial review of PR #67, round 2 (F038's surrogate fail-open fix). Not a currently-known-open bypass -- the reviewer who raised it explicitly judged the two specific fixes already shipped (F038 rounds 2-3) as 'complete for the branch [they] target' after checking the entire relevant codepoint space. This is defense-in-depth against the NEXT unknown exception type in the same decoder, not a fix for a known-live bug -- deliberately not folded into F038's own emergency-fix PRs, which were already at their third round under time pressure from a live regression.

FIXED with two layers, since the actual call graph turned out wider than the ticket's own "per-target scan" framing: _flag_view() (used throughout cp_mv_targets()/sed_inplace_targets()/all_flagless_tokens() for flag/command-name RECOGNITION, not target extraction) calls the SAME unquote_token()/_decode_ansi_c_escape() decoder on every token it inspects, well BEFORE write_targets()'s own final target-decode line ever runs -- meaning for cp/mv/tee/rm/sed targets, a decoder crash fires during recognition, not at the final per-target step the ticket described. Layer 1: write_targets()'s final unquote_token() pass is now applied per-target (try/except per token, falling back to that token's raw text), reachable specifically for PLAIN redirect targets (> />>), which bypass every earlier _flag_view() call. Layer 2: main()'s per-segment loop now wraps the WHOLE write_targets(segment) call, falling back to the raw segment text as a single pseudo-target on ANY exception -- this is what actually protects cp/mv/tee/rm/sed targets (where the crash happens during recognition, before layer 1 ever gets a chance) and, critically, prevents a crash in ONE segment of a compound command from killing the check of a LATER segment (e.g. after `;`). Both fallbacks deliberately only apply to TARGET-VALUE decode failures, not FLAG-recognition ones (_flag_view() itself was NOT given a raw-text fallback): falling back to raw text for a FLAG comparison would risk silently disabling a real -i/--in-place/script-value guard (a fail-OPEN), the opposite safety direction from a target-value decode failure (which is safe-directional -- a raw, still-escaped string essentially never matches a real scope prefix, so it's very likely DENIED, not allowed). [SUPERSEDED, see ROUND 2 below -- "essentially never matches a real scope prefix" is FALSE for attacker-chosen input: the attacker controls the raw fallback text and can place the crash immediately after a valid scope prefix, confirmed as a live bypass by adversarial review, not merely a documentation inaccuracy.] Verified with a deliberately fault-injected test fixture (a copy of enforce-scope.sh where _decode_ansi_c_escape() raises for the otherwise-inert "\Q" escape, simulating F038's own two real crashers without depending on a live 0-day existing today), since no live decoder crash currently exists -- the reviewer who raised this ticket had already confirmed the two known exception types are fully closed. Mutation-tested each layer in isolation: reverting layer 1 alone produces a coarser (but still safe) segment-level denial, caught by a dedicated discriminating assertion; reverting layer 2 alone reproduces the EXACT fail-open the ticket describes (uncaught traceback, empty stdout, silent ALLOW of a real out-of-scope write) -- confirmed via the actual Python traceback surfacing during the mutation run. [Round 1's two-layer design itself was replaced in round 2 -- see below.]

ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #73): round 1's fallback -- comparing attacker-controlled raw/undecoded text (either one target's raw token, or the whole raw segment) against scope patterns -- was a REAL BYPASS, not just an inaccurate comment. The attacker chooses where the crash lands, and can trivially place it immediately AFTER an in-scope-looking prefix (e.g. "src/parser/"), making the raw fallback text itself look in-scope. Confirmed live: `src/parser/$'\Qx' > src/other/evil.txt` silently ALLOWed the real out-of-scope redirect under round 1 -- using the exact same construction round 1's OWN tests used to prove "processing continues past the crash", which in hindsight built the bypass into the fixture as a convenience without recognizing it IS the attack. FIXED by replacing BOTH round-1 layers with one unified per-segment try/except (main()'s own _check_segment() helper) that denies UNCONDITIONALLY on any analysis failure -- never comparing any fallback text against scope patterns at all, since there is no text to fall back to that isn't equally attacker-controlled. This is a strictly SIMPLER design than round 1's two-layer split (no more per-target vs per-segment distinction, no more raw-text scope comparison) and closes a SEPARATE gap the same review found: the final denial `print(f"Bash write to '{norm}' is outside...")` call crashes with UnicodeEncodeError if `norm` ever contains a raw lone surrogate -- this is the ACTUAL F038 round-2 incident (a surrogate reaching PRINT/json.dumps(), not a ValueError from chr() itself, which round 1's own comment mislabeled) -- that print() call now sits INSIDE the same try/except, not a separate uncovered path. Also added a one-line stderr diagnostic note (round 1 made a decoder crash completely silent; before ANY of this work, a crash left a visible Python traceback on stderr). Re-verified both original F1 counterexamples now correctly DENY, re-ran the full mutation-test suite against the new single try/except (revert -> exactly 6 of 12 F042 assertions fail, all crash-related, none of the no-crash/no-regression ones), full suite 1076/1076 green. Also fixed a separate test-harness defect the same review found (F3): the fault-injection setup's own exit status was previously ignored (run-tests.sh has `set -u` but not `set -e`), so a broken injection marker would silently leave the fixture running the PRISTINE hook and every F042 assertion would still pass, testing nothing -- confirmed this exact failure mode live before fixing it with an explicit `|| fail ...` gate.
approaches_tried: Round 1: tried a two-layer raw-text fallback (per-target decode fallback in write_targets(), per-segment fallback in main()), each comparing attacker-controlled fallback text against scope patterns on a decoder exception. Ground-truthed with a deliberately fault-injected decoder (a copy of enforce-scope.sh raising for the otherwise-inert "\Q" escape) since no live decoder crash exists today. Adversarial review found this was a genuine live bypass (attacker places the crash right after a valid scope prefix, making the fallback text itself look in-scope), not just an inaccurate comment -- DISCARDED in favor of round 2.

Round 2: replaced both layers with a single unified per-segment try/except (_check_segment() in main()) that denies UNCONDITIONALLY on any analysis failure, never comparing fallback text against scope at all. Strictly simpler than round 1 (one code path instead of two, no raw-text scope comparison) and closes a second gap the same review found (the denial print() itself could crash on a raw surrogate, outside either round-1 layer). Re-verified both round-1 counterexamples now deny; mutation-tested the single try/except (revert -> exactly 6 of 12 F042 assertions fail, all crash-related).

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's FILE_PATH/COMMAND extraction (the `FILE_PATH=$(echo "$INPUT" | python3 -c "..." 2>/dev/null)` block) fails open the same way _decode_ansi_c_escape() did before F038 rounds 2-3, but earlier in the pipeline and via a different entry point: a raw lone UTF-16 surrogate (0xD800-0xDFFF) arriving directly in the hook's OWN input JSON (e.g. `{"tool_input":{"file_path":"src/other/\ud800pwned.txt"}}` -- no $'...' ANSI-C quoting or bash decoding involved at all, since json.load() itself decodes the JSON \uD800 escape into a Python str containing a lone surrogate) crashes `print(path)` with the same UnicodeEncodeError. The `2>/dev/null` on that command substitution swallows the traceback, FILE_PATH comes back empty, and `if [ -n "$FILE_PATH" ]` skips the ENTIRE Edit/Write scope check block -- silently allowing what should have gone through the AUTHORITATIVE file_path gate (Edit/Write/MultiEdit tool calls are blocked outright, not best-effort like the Bash coverage path F038 itself patches). The identical extraction pattern is used for COMMAND just below it, so the Bash coverage path is affected too.

features.notes:
Discovered by adversarial review of PR #67, round 2 (F038's surrogate/multi-char-uppercase fixes for the $'...' ANSI-C decoder). Pre-dates F038 entirely -- this is a structurally different code path (the hook's own top-level JSON input extraction, not the bash-side $'...' decoder F038 touches) with much lower reachability, since a lone surrogate must survive transport from whatever produces the tool_input JSON in the first place (Claude's own model output is valid UTF-8/UTF-16 text and would not normally carry an isolated surrogate this way; some other JSON-producing intermediary would need to construct or forward one). Deliberately not folded into F038's own PRs, which were already at their third round under time pressure from a live regression in a different function -- filed as its own feature per the round-2 reviewer's explicit recommendation.

FIXED: confirmed the bypass live before touching code (both a raw \uD800 surrogate in tool_input.file_path AND in tool_input.command produced rc=0 with completely empty stdout -- silent ALLOW -- against a fixture scoped to src/parser/, while the identical non-surrogate command correctly denied). Fixed with a two-stage try/except per extraction script, using TWO DISTINCT exit codes rather than one: exit 2 means json.load() itself failed (genuinely unparseable input, stays fail-open -- this file's own documented environment-failure contract, unchanged), exit 1 means the JSON parsed successfully but something after that (the field extraction, normalize, or the final print()) crashed (fails closed). A single except-and-exit(1) wrapping BOTH stages would have silently reversed the documented fail-open behavior for genuinely malformed JSON, since Python's default uncaught-exception exit code is 1 regardless of which stage raised -- confirmed this exact regression live via a dedicated mutation test (collapsing the two stages into one flipped the 'genuinely unparseable JSON stays fail-open' test from ALLOW to DENY). FILE_PATH's denial uses the plain-text/exit-2 form (matching its existing authoritative-gate convention); COMMAND's uses deny_json() (matching its existing best-effort-gate convention) -- neither introduces a new denial format into a code path that didn't already have one. Mutation-tested the whole fix (revert -> exactly 4 of 7 new assertions fail) and the two-stage design specifically (collapse to one stage -> exactly 1 assertion fails, the malformed-JSON regression test) in isolation.

features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's command-name recognition (write_targets()'s cp/mv/tee/rm dispatch, sed_inplace_targets()'s own sed-name guard) fully closed F040's quoting/backslash-escaping gap, but command-name INDIRECTION is a separate, still-open bypass on the same call sites: `/bin/rm`, `./rm`, `sudo rm`, `env rm`, `command rm`, `xargs rm`, and `FOO=1 rm` are all wrongly ALLOWED (no target extracted at all), since none of these tokens equals the bare command-name strings the dispatch compares against, even after _flag_view() normalization. CONFIRMED live (F040 PR #69 review): `FOO=1 rm src/other/h.txt` really deletes the out-of-scope file in real bash, and the hook allows it silently on both main (pre-F040) and the F040 branch (post-fix) alike -- this bug is pre-existing and outside F040's scope, not a regression it introduced. Arguably wider than F040 itself, since it defeats the SAME extractors via a completely different evasion class (indirection rather than quoting). Precedent for a fix already exists in this repo: skills/harness-init/commit-gate.sh.template's is_git_token() handles the path form via `os.path.basename(tok.lstrip("(\\"))`; the env-var-prefix and wrapper-command forms (sudo/env/command/xargs) would need their own handling.

features.notes:
Discovered by adversarial review of PR #69 (F040), while sweeping for other command-recognition bypasses in the same functions F040 just fixed. Confirmed live pre- and post-F040 (pre-existing, not a regression): /bin/rm, ./rm, sudo rm, env rm, command rm, xargs rm, FOO=1 rm all silently bypass write_targets()'s cp/mv/tee/rm recognition entirely.

FIXED: built _resolve_command_tokens(), mirroring commit-gate.sh's is_git_token() path-form precedent (os.path.basename() after stripping a leading subshell-paren/backslash) and extending it with wrapper-command resolution (sudo/env/command/xargs, each followed by its own leading flags, also skipped) and env-assignment-prefix resolution (one or more VAR=value tokens). Confirmed against real bash before writing any fix: /bin/rm, FOO=1 rm, command rm, env rm, and xargs rm (piped a filename) all genuinely delete the target file; sudo rm is the same immediate-exec mechanism as command/env and not separately re-verified since this repo's own sandbox has no sudo access. Refactored sed_inplace_targets() to take args (the tokens after the resolved command name) directly rather than re-deriving its own narrower sed-name check internally (which only recognized F040's quoting/escaping, not indirection) -- write_targets()'s dispatch and sed_inplace_targets() now share ONE resolution instead of risking two inconsistent copies, the same lesson F041 already established for its own shared _sed_consumes_next_as_script() predicate. Bounded the resolver's own walk by len(tokens) so an all-wrapper token list (e.g. 'env command' with no real command after it) can't loop indefinitely -- confirmed live it correctly resolves to no targets (ALLOW, no crash) rather than erroring. Ran the full existing 1083-assertion suite BEFORE writing any new tests to confirm the dispatch refactor was behavior-preserving for every previously-tested case (zero regressions), then added 22 new assertions across 11 bypass shapes (path-form, sudo, env with flags, command, xargs, single and multiple env-assignment prefixes, cp/sed via the same resolver, a chained wrapper) plus 4 no-false-positive/no-crash assertions. Mutation-tested by reverting the whole template to the pre-fix version (via the parent commit) with the new tests still in place: exactly 22 failures, all F044-tagged, matching the 11 bypass tests precisely and nothing else. [SUPERSEDED: the assertion count was wrong -- see ROUND 2 below. "22" was actually the count of assertions that fail on a full revert (each bypass test's own rc0 assertion trivially passes whether ALLOW or DENY, since rc is 0 either way), not the total number of NEW assertions added, which was 41.]

ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #76): one real, live bypass INSIDE the round-1 fix's own stated contract, plus two documentation/metadata accuracy items. (1) BLOCKING: the wrapper-flag skip only ever consumed ONE token per flag, so a flag whose value is a SEPARATE argument (`sudo -u root`, `xargs -n 1`, `env -u FOO`, `env -C /tmp`) was wrongly treated as making the flag's OWN VALUE the command name -- silently allowing the real wrapped command. Confirmed live against real bash that each genuinely deletes the target file, and confirmed the round-1 code's own comment ("followed by its OWN leading flags, also skipped") was true only for the attached form. FIXED: added WRAPPER_VALUE_FLAGS (a per-wrapper set of short flags sourced from this platform's own sudo/env/xargs --help output plus the reviewer's own cross-checked list, explicitly disclosed as not exhaustively verified across every GNU/Linux version) and skip an extra token when one is encountered. Mutation-tested in isolation: reverting ONLY this fix (keeping everything else from round 1) reproduces exactly 6 failures across exactly the 3 separate-arg-value tests, nothing else. (2) COMMAND_WRAPPERS not exhaustive (nohup/exec/nice/time/setsid/stdbuf/timeout/busybox/doas all still bypass) -- explicitly disclosed in the code comment as a scope decision, not silently assumed complete; extending the wrapper list further is a candidate for its own future feature if warranted. (3) The "22 new assertions" claim in round 1 was wrong (actual count was 41; 22 is how many fail on full revert, since each test's own rc0 assertion passes for both ALLOW and DENY) -- corrected above, marked SUPERSEDED rather than silently rewritten. Round 2 added 14 more assertions (55 total added across both rounds); full suite 1138/1138 green.

ROUND 3 (adversarial review of PR #76 round 2): APPROVE was conditional on correcting a residual comment that understated the gap -- the note scoped its residual to "any flag this set is missing" (a short-flag inventory gap), but TWO ENTIRE SHAPES were unhandled: a clustered short flag ending in a value-taking one (`env -iu FOO rm`, `xargs -0n 1 rm`) and a long option given its value as a separate argument (`xargs --max-args 1 rm`, `env --unset FOO rm`). Confirmed live against real bash that all four examples genuinely delete the target file: `env -iu FOO rm`, `xargs -0n 1 rm`, and `xargs --max-args 1 rm` on this platform's own /usr/bin/env and /usr/bin/xargs; `env --unset FOO rm` specifically against GNU coreutils (Homebrew genv), since BSD/macOS's own /usr/bin/env has no --unset at all (confirmed: `/usr/bin/env --unset FOO echo test` errors "No such file or directory", rc=127, not a real unset-and-exec) -- a real gap on GNU/Linux, just not reproducible with this machine's stock env binary (found by post-merge re-verification, PR #76). The reviewer explicitly offered a choice between widening the disclaimer (minimum, already sufficient for approval) or fixing both shapes (estimated ~3 lines plus 4 tests); chose to fix both since they were cheap, mechanical, and confirmed-live rather than hypothetical, matching this sweep's established practice of closing real gaps rather than only documenting around them once found. FIXED: added _is_wrapper_value_flag(), which handles an exact match (now including long-option spellings alongside the existing short ones in WRAPPER_VALUE_FLAGS) OR a clustered short-flag token whose LAST character is itself a value-taking flag. Mutation-tested both sub-mechanisms independently: reverting the clustering check alone (exact-match-only call site, long-form entries still present) fails exactly the 2 clustered-flag tests (4 assertions); reverting the long-form entries alone (keeping the clustering logic, short-only WRAPPER_VALUE_FLAGS) fails exactly the 2 long-option tests (4 assertions) -- confirming both additions are independently load-bearing, not redundant with each other. Full suite 1155/1155 green (17 more assertions added this round, 72 total across all three rounds).

features.description: skills/harness-init/commit-gate.sh.template's is_git_token() recognizes a LEADING-backslash form (`\git`), `(git`, and path forms like `/usr/bin/git`, but NOT a quoted command name (`"git"` or `'git'`) [the leading-backslash claim is leading-only, not interior escapes -- see ROUND 2 in notes] -- the mirror-image of the gap F040 just closed in enforce-scope.sh's command-name recognition. CONFIRMED at the function level: extracting is_git_token() and unit-testing it directly shows `"git"` -> False and `'git'` -> False (should be True). NOT YET CONFIRMED end-to-end through the real hook: a plain `git commit -m x` (the simplest possible input) did not trigger the gate at all in the reviewer's fixture during the F040 PR #69 review, so reachability of this specific quoted-command-name gap through the actual commit-gate.sh entry point is unverified -- flagged as likely, not confirmed, pending a dedicated fixture that first establishes a baseline case where the gate demonstrably fires.

features.notes:
Discovered by adversarial review of PR #69 (F040), as a sibling-file check for the same command-name-recognition bug class F040 just fixed in enforce-scope.sh. Reviewer explicitly could not confirm end-to-end reachability (the gate itself did not fire on a plain `git commit -m x` in their fixture) -- first task for whoever picks this up is establishing why the gate isn't firing at all before assessing the quoted-name gap's real severity.

RESOLVED (not a bug): first task per this entry's own notes was establishing why the gate didn't fire on a plain `git commit -m x` before assessing the quoted-name gap's severity -- answer: that command is NOT supposed to trigger a denial at all. It's exactly the SAFE, repaired pattern the gate's own repair message recommends (`git add` separately, then a plain `git commit` with no staging flags) -- the earlier reviewer's fixture was testing a non-violation, not evidence the gate was broken. Re-tested with an actual violation (`git commit -a -m wip`, which correctly denies with the compound-stage-and-commit reason) and its quoted-git-name variants (`"git" commit -a -m wip`, `'git' commit -a -m wip`): BOTH quoted forms ALREADY deny identically to the bare form, end-to-end, live. Read why: parse_command()'s own comment states tokens are unquoted ONE AT A TIME via unquote_token() immediately after split_tokens(seg), BEFORE segment_subcommand() (the function that calls is_git_token()) ever sees them (`tokens = [unquote_token(t) for t in split_tokens(seg)]`). So by the time is_git_token() is actually invoked in the real pipeline, a quoted "git"/'git' is indistinguishable from bare git -- the original ticket's "unit-level test" (feeding is_git_token() a RAW, still-quoted string in isolation) tested a call shape that never occurs in the real pipeline, since is_git_token() has exactly ONE call site and it always receives an already-unquoted token. No code change needed FOR THE QUOTED-COMMAND-NAME GAP SPECIFICALLY -- see ROUND 2 below for a separate, more severe live bypass the same review found in the same function's surrounding machinery. Added 2 regression tests (6 assertions) documenting this invariant. Mutation-tested by reverting parse_command()'s own pre-unquote step: 13 assertions failed (4 from the new F045 tests, 9 pre-existing). Round-3 review (self-correction after round-2's own figure was found wrong on a THIRD pass) confirmed the 9 pre-existing F025 assertions ALONE already catch this mutation: removing the 2 new F045 tests and re-applying the same parse_command()-pre-unquote revert fails 9 assertions (1146/1155) -- the lead's own first attempt to reproduce this got 12 (a test-harness fixture-pollution artifact of a crude text-splice removal method, confirmed spurious by testing the exact plain-git secret-scan case directly against the isolated hook, which still correctly denied under the mutation). Separately, a second mutation feeding segment_subcommand() raw tokens directly -- the exact "future refactor" scenario these tests were justified by -- fails 12 assertions (1149/1161), 8 of them pre-existing. So the new tests' own rationale ("guards against a future refactor reopening this gap") doesn't fully hold on its own merits, since that specific refactor is already caught without them. Kept anyway: 6 assertions is a negligible cost and they directly document the quoted-git-name invariant from its own angle (F025's tests document the quoted-subcommand angle, a related but distinct claim) -- correcting the over-claim here rather than removing tests that still have documentation value, per the reviewer's own recommendation.

ROUND 2 (adversarial review of PR #77): while confirming this entry's own "not a bug" conclusion, the reviewer found a SEPARATE, far more severe live bypass in the same is_git_token()/unquote_token() machinery: commit-gate.sh.template's own unquote_token() strips a $'...' ANSI-C-quote wrapper with a plain regex substitution and never decodes escapes inside it, and never strips a bare interior backslash either -- unlike enforce-scope.sh's own unquote_token(), which F038 already hardened to decode ANSI-C escapes. Confirmed live (independently reproduced before acting): `g\it commit -a -m "test"`, `\g\i\t commit -a -m "test"`, and `$'\x67it' commit -a -m "test"` all silently ALLOW where the bare `git commit -a -m "test"` correctly denies (compound-stage-and-commit) -- and with a staged secret, `g\it commit -m "add config"` bypasses the SECRET-SCAN check entirely too (bare `git commit -m "add config"` correctly denies secret-assignment; the escaped form silently allows the commit through). This is because is_git_token() failing makes segment_subcommand() return (None, None), which skips BOTH the compound check and the secret scan, not just one -- the same severity class as F025 (a full, silent gate no-op). `\"git\"` (backslash before a quote) is a benign exception -- it produces the literal word `"git"`, which real bash reports as command-not-found, not a bypass. Filed separately (not fixed in this PR, which stays scoped to the quoted-name question this entry was originally about) as its own, higher-priority feature -- see F051.

features.description: skills/harness-init/check-remaining-tasks.sh.template (the TeammateIdle blocking hook) exits 2 to keep an idle teammate working, but writes its guidance text (which feature to pick up, or the retrospective/wrap-up instruction) to STDOUT, never stderr. CONFIRMED live: `echo '{}' | bash .claude/hooks/check-remaining-tasks.sh 2>/dev/null` prints the full guidance message; the same command with `2>&1 1>/dev/null` (stderr only) prints nothing at all, rc=2. [SUPERSEDED, see CORRECTION in notes below: this sibling-hook comparison was ground-truthed as FALSE during review -- all three sibling hooks write their blocking guidance to stdout too, not stderr] Every sibling blocking hook writes its guidance to stderr instead (`grep -c '>&2'`: enforce-scope.sh.template=2, verify-task-quality.sh.template=3), and this appears to be the channel the harness actually surfaces back to a blocked teammate -- a teammate held idle by this hook receives an empty message on every re-prompt and has no way to learn what work it's being asked to pick up, and no way to tell whether the loop is expected to keep firing or is stuck. Reachable by any teammate that finishes its assigned work while claimable features remain in features.json (e.g. a reviewer with no further review to do), which is an ordinary, non-adversarial outcome, not an edge case.

features.notes:

Independently confirmed live before filing: the hook's guidance text is genuinely only on stdout, stderr is empty on every invocation. Also flagged by the same reporter: this doesn't fully solve idle teammates with no assignable work (e.g. reviewers) -- the hook has no concept of role and will re-block ANY idle teammate for as long as ANY feature is claimable, which is a separate design question (role-aware idle behavior), not addressed by this fix. FIXED: both echo statements in check-remaining-tasks.sh.template's final claimable-feature branch now write to stderr (`>&2`), matching the sibling hooks' convention. Ground-truthed the bug directly before fixing (stdout-only run showed the full guidance; stderr-only run was completely empty, rc=2) and re-verified the fix the same way (stdout-only now empty, stderr-only carries the guidance). Updated the one existing test that asserted against combined stdout (`run_hook` doesn't capture stderr unless the caller redirects it, so this test would have silently gone green on empty output without the `2>&1` fix) and added 2 new assertions that pin the fix specifically: stdout must be empty, and the claimable feature id must appear when only stderr is captured. Full suite 1193/1193. Mutation-tested by reverting to the pre-fix template: exactly the 2 new assertions fail, nothing else.

CORRECTION (review of PR #80): the FIXED paragraph above, and the description field's `grep -c '>&2'` comparison, both claimed the sibling hooks (enforce-scope.sh.template, verify-task-quality.sh.template) already write their blocking guidance to stderr. Ground-truthed and confirmed FALSE: the `>&2` counts quoted in the description are comment lines and progress-log lines, not blocking guidance -- both of enforce-scope.sh.template's `exit 2` sites (:166, :212) and all four of verify-task-quality.sh.template's (:47, :81, :92, :125), plus verify-git-identity.sh.template's one (:68), write their actual rejection/block message via plain `echo` to stdout. This fix is correct, but for a different, now-verified reason: per Claude Code's own docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks, confirmed via direct fetch), exit 2 discards a hook's stdout entirely and feeds only stderr back to the blocked agent as its error message -- this was the FIRST hook in this repo to get that channel right, not one matching an existing convention. Comment in the template and this notes field corrected accordingly. Filed F053 (discovered_via F046) for the identical defect in the three sibling hooks, since PreToolUse/Stop/SubagentStop/TeammateIdle are all confirmed exit-2-discards-stdout paths, but TaskCompleted's exit-2 semantics were not independently confirmed and need checking before scoping that fix.
