features.description: skills/harness-init/enforce-scope.sh.template's sed_inplace_targets() only checks the FILE being edited (`sed -i<SUFFIX> ... file`) against scope, never the backup-suffix value itself, even though GNU sed's `*` expansion in the suffix lets the backup land in a completely different (potentially out-of-scope) directory. CONFIRMED against real gsed 4.10, executed from an in-scope `src/parser/` cwd: `gsed -i'../other/*' 's/a/b/' p.txt` genuinely creates a real file at `../other/p.txt` (rc=0), and the identical gap exists for the long form `--in-place=../other/*`. The hook extracts only `p.txt` (correctly recognized as in scope) and never inspects the suffix value at all, so the actual out-of-scope backup write goes completely unchecked. Present identically on main and on the F041 PR (#71) HEAD -- pre-existing, not introduced by F041's abbreviation fix, and a different bug class entirely (a second, unchecked write target hiding inside a flag's OWN value, not a flag-recognition gap).

features.notes:
Discovered by adversarial review of PR #71 (F041 round 2), while differentially fuzzing sed_inplace_targets() against an independent GNU-sed parsing model (406,900+ sequences) to look for any remaining fail-open in the abbreviation fix. Explicitly flagged by the reviewer as its own, different bug class (a second write target -- the backup file -- rather than a flag-recognition gap) and recommended as a separate feature rather than folding into F041. Independently confirmed live before filing: `gsed -i'../other/*' 's/a/b/' p.txt` from an in-scope cwd genuinely writes outside scope.

FIXED: added _is_inplace_flag() (a single shared predicate for "is this the in-place flag", replacing the presence check's inline duplicated condition, to avoid a guard-vs-loop disagreement risk this file has hit before -- F029/F052/F041) and _sed_inplace_suffix_raw() (extracts the RAW, not-yet-unquoted suffix attached to an in-place flag, mirroring _attached_value_raw()'s technique so the derived target is unquoted exactly once later by write_targets(), never twice -- the exact double-unquote bug class F035 rounds 2/3 fixed for cp_mv_targets()). Ground-truthed against real GNU sed 4.10 before implementing: only the LAST in-place-enabling flag's suffix matters (a later -i entirely overrides an earlier one's suffix, not just its presence -- confirmed both directions: a later suffixed -i replaces an earlier one, and a later BARE -i cancels an earlier suffix entirely, no backup at all); a suffix with no "*" is always either empty or a literal string GNU sed appends directly to the file argument (confirmed this holds even when that literal suffix itself contains "/", which produces a malformed concatenated path real GNU sed's own rename immediately rejects -- documented as an accepted, vanishingly narrow residual, not fixed); a suffix WITH "*" always needs checking, even with no "/" of its own, since the file argument itself may carry directory components that get baked into the substitution in a scope-relevant way (confirmed directly: `sed -iBACKUP_'*' file` from within a subdirectory attempts to rename into a sibling directory literally named after the file's own path prefix). Added 16 new assertions covering: attached and long-form asterisk suffixes, multiple files (each gets its own derived target), last-flag-wins for both a later suffix replacing an earlier one AND a later bare -i cancelling one, plus two no-false-positive controls (an ordinary no-asterisk suffix, and an asterisk-bearing suffix whose derived path is still in scope). Full suite 1229/1229. Mutation-tested by reverting to the pre-fix template (and its resynced live copy): exactly 6 failures (the discriminating deny-related assertions for the 4 bypass-shape tests), both negative-control tests correctly unaffected.

ROUND 2 (review of PR #83): reviewer ground-truthed all four core GNU sed claims independently against real gsed 4.10, ran a 225-case differential fuzz against real gsed with zero mismatches, and swept 10,290 asterisk-free invocations comparing main against this branch with zero differences (confirming no new false positives on ordinary sed usage). Found one new residual: the "*" PRESENCE check reads the DECODED view but the substitution operates on the RAW string, so an ANSI-C-escaped asterisk (a suffix given as $'\x2a') is invisible to .replace("*", tok) -- the derived target ends up as a bare, undecoded "*" instead of the true substituted path. Independently reproduced by the lead before fixing. Confirmed over-deny only, never a bypass (the derived and true strings always share the same prefix up to the first "*", and scope matching is a plain prefix check with no globbing) -- documented as an accepted residual, matching this file's existing pattern for other narrow, safe-directional gaps, rather than restructuring the RAW/decoded-value handling for an edge case this narrow. Added 1 regression test locking in the over-deny direction. Full suite after fix: 1231/1231.
approaches_tried: extract the RAW backup-suffix value from whichever flag position enables in-place editing (last one wins, matching real GNU sed), and whenever it contains "*", derive a second write target by substituting the RAW file token for every "*", mirroring cp_mv_targets()'s own RAW-value-extraction convention to avoid double-unquoting

features.description: The identical raw-lone-surrogate extraction fail-open F043 fixed in enforce-scope.sh.template's FILE_PATH/COMMAND extraction is ALSO present, unfixed, in commit-gate.sh.template's and verify-git-identity.sh.template's own `COMMAND=$(echo "$INPUT" | python3 -c "...json.load...print(...)" 2>/dev/null)` blocks -- both are gating hooks (not best-effort), so this is a full bypass, not a coverage gap. CONFIRMED live: `git commit -a -m wip` is correctly DENIED by commit-gate.sh (compound-stage-and-commit reason), but the identical command with a trailing \uD800 in the message (`git commit -a -m wip\ud800`) exits rc=0 with completely empty output -- the pre-commit secret-scan gate is silently bypassed by one character. The same pattern (same code, same fix needed) is also present in verify-git-identity.sh.template's own git-identity-mismatch gate (reviewer confirmed this one live too), and, lower priority, in verify-task-quality.sh.template and hooks/session-start.sh. verify-task-quality.sh.template's own coverage gate DOES gate (a rejection exits 2), but its low priority is NOT because it's non-gating -- reviewer confirmed live that a surrogate reaches it only via metadata.feature_id, which is printed unvalidated, and buys an attacker nothing a bogus or simply omitted feature_id doesn't already buy (both also silently skip the whole gate, confirmed live: `metadata.feature_id: "F999bogus"` and no feature_id at all both give rc=0 same as the surrogate case) -- the coverage gate is self-reported and already trivially skippable by construction, so closing the surrogate specifically here would be a false sense of soundness, not a real fix, unless the broader self-reporting gap is addressed too. check-remaining-tasks.sh.template was REMOVED from this feature's scope (reviewer confirmed live it does not have the pattern at all: its own extraction has no `2>/dev/null` at all, a crash there prints a real traceback rather than being silently swallowed, and it already exits 2 unconditionally regardless of whether its result is empty -- the input also comes from harness_state.py over lead-owned features.json, not attacker-controlled tool input). [SUPERSEDED, see FIXED in notes below: hooks/session-start.sh was ultimately excluded from this feature's scope -- it documents "Always exits 0; never blocks" and has no fail-closed state to reach] The fix for the two gating hooks and hooks/session-start.sh is mechanically the same two-stage try/except (exit 2 = JSON unparseable, stays fail-open; exit 1 = parsed fine but unsafe to process further, fails closed) F043 already wrote and ground-truthed for enforce-scope.sh.template.

Independently confirmed live (by the lead, not just the reviewer) for commit-gate.sh.template before filing: control `git commit -a -m wip` denies with the compound-stage-and-commit reason; the identical command with a trailing surrogate exits rc=0 with empty output. Note this fix does not protect THIS repo's own live .claude/hooks/*.sh until F047 (the live-hooks-out-of-sync resync) also lands -- the two are independent but related.

Round 2 of PR #74's review (after F043 merged) found two accuracy nits in this entry's own text, both confirmed live before applying: (1) verify-task-quality.sh.template's low priority is because its coverage gate is already trivially skippable via a bogus/omitted feature_id, not because it's non-gating -- corrected so a future implementer doesn't think fixing the surrogate alone makes the gate sound. (2) check-remaining-tasks.sh.template does not have this pattern at all (no 2>/dev/null, unconditional exit 2, lead-owned input source) -- removed from scope.

FIXED: applied the same two-stage exit-code split F043 wrote for enforce-scope.sh.template to commit-gate.sh.template's and verify-git-identity.sh.template's COMMAND extraction (exit 2 = unparseable JSON stays fail-open; exit 1 = parsed fine but crashed afterward, fails closed), and to verify-task-quality.sh.template's FEATURE_ID extraction (same split, but WITHOUT giving a crash any new blocking power -- consistent with the round-1 correction above about this hook's coverage gate already being trivially skippable). verify-git-identity.sh.template's fix is deliberately placed AFTER its existing "is an identity even configured" checks (moved the harness.json/EXPECTED_NAME/EXPECTED_EMAIL block earlier in the file), so a crash only ever blocks once there is a real identity to protect -- ground-truthed this ordering choice directly: a project with no configured identity still allows a surrogate-bearing command exactly as before. hooks/session-start.sh was excluded from the fix entirely after reading its own header: it explicitly documents 'Always exits 0; never blocks', so there is no fail-closed state to achieve for a hook that never gates anything -- its existing `|| true` posture is already the correct behavior, not a residual bug. Re-verified all three fixes against real live scenarios before writing tests (control case still denies/blocks correctly, surrogate variant now denies/blocks too, genuinely unparseable JSON stays fail-open). Added 14 new assertions across the three files (commit-gate: 5, verify-git-identity: 4, verify-task-quality: 5). Full suite 1245/1245. Mutation-tested by reverting all three templates and their resynced live copies: exactly 5 failures (the discriminating assertions, one set per file), every negative-control test (no-identity-configured, valid-feature_id, genuinely-unparseable-JSON) correctly unaffected.
approaches_tried: port the identical two-stage try/except pattern F043 already wrote for enforce-scope.sh.template to the two gating hooks (commit-gate.sh, verify-git-identity.sh), and to verify-task-quality.sh's non-gating FEATURE_ID extraction for consistency without changing its accept/reject verdict; excluded hooks/session-start.sh after confirming it never blocks by design

features.description: skills/harness-init/commit-gate.sh.template's compound-stage-and-commit check (DENY_COMPOUND) only looks for staging flags (-a/-i/--all/--include) or a separate `git add`/`git stage` in the same command -- it never considers a bare pathspec argument on `git commit` itself. `git commit -m x tracked.txt` and `git commit -m x -- tracked.txt` both commit the WORKING-TREE content of the named file directly, without ever touching the index, exactly like `-a` does for the whole tree -- confirmed against real git (a modified-but-unstaged tracked.txt is committed with its dirty content, `git diff --cached` shows nothing staged beforehand). Because the secret scan (Check 1) only reads `git diff --cached`, a secret introduced this way is invisible to it, identically to the -a/-i bypass DENY_COMPOUND exists to block -- except has_staging_flag() never looks for a bare pathspec at all. Confirmed this behaves identically on main and on both F051 rounds (not a regression from that work). Found by adversarial review of PR #79 (F051 round 2).

features.notes:
Discovered by review-pr79-f051 while re-verifying the F051 round-2 fix; independently reproduced by the lead against a fresh fixture before filing (git commit -m x tracked.txt on a dirty tracked file with a secret-shaped line commits it, hook silently allows, `git diff --cached` before the commit is empty -- confirmed identical on main and F051 round 2, so not a regression). Filed separately rather than folding into F051 to keep that PR's diff scoped to the reviewer's original CHANGES NEEDED finding.

FIXED: extended has_staging_flag() (kept the name to avoid an unnecessary rename ripple through every call site and test) to also flag any flagless token that survives past the existing flag/value-skip logic as a bare pathspec -- both before a real "--" separator and unconditionally after one, since real git commit never uses a "--"-separated argument as an opaque value for anything. This flipped the expected outcome for three PRE-EXISTING tests that previously asserted ALLOW for a trailing pathspec (each was actually testing a narrower property -- that the pathspec wasn't misread AS a staging flag, which remains true -- but the overall command is now correctly denied for the broader F052 reason instead): the F051r2 real-separator test, the 'git commit -- -a.txt' case in the attached-value-flags loop, and the ambiguous '--t -- -a' abbreviation test (the latter is now an accepted, safe-directional over-denial, since real git errors on the ambiguous --t before ever reaching '-- -a' at all -- the hook can't know that without fully modeling git's own option-ambiguity detection, and over-denial here is consistent with this file's existing posture for ambiguous/ill-formed input). Also updated the header's stale 'Residual holes' comment, which still described this exact gap as unfixed. Added 14 new assertions: the core bug (bare pathspec, no '--' at all), multiple pathspecs, two no-false-positive controls (ordinary no-pathspec commit, --amend --no-edit), plus the three updated tests' new DENY assertions. Full suite 1256/1256. Mutation-tested by reverting to the pre-fix template (and its resynced live copy): exactly 7 failures (the discriminating assertions across all 4 updated/new test groups), every no-false-positive control correctly unaffected.

ROUND 2 (review of PR #85): reviewer independently reproduced the core bug and all three test-expectation flips against real git 2.52.0, ran a 20-command false-positive battery, and mutation-tested in an isolated scratch clone (1249/1256, exactly 7 failures, matching round 1's own claim). Two required fixes, both accuracy issues, no logic errors: (1) DENY_COMPOUND's repair message still only named -a/-i/--all/--include, giving no hint that a trailing pathspec (this feature's own new trigger) was the actual reason -- corrected to mention dropping any trailing pathspec too. (2) _flag_view()'s own comment claimed an unquoted-and-escaped `\--` with nothing after it 'falls through as an ordinary non-flag token, extending the scan' -- no longer true post-F052 (verified live: `git commit -m x \--` denies on this branch, allowed on main): it now hits the new bare-pathspec check and returns True immediately, an accepted over-denial (never a bypass, confirmed) via a different mechanism than the comment described -- corrected. Also cleaned up the header's 'Residual holes' entry (it contradicted its own heading by listing a FIXED item under it), simplified `i += 1; i += 1` to `i += 2` per the reviewer's own note that it read like a bug, and added a test for a genuine additional bypass shape the fix already closed but nothing tested: `--untracked-files` is an optarg long flag that only takes an ATTACHED value, so a bare `--untracked-files no` reads 'no' as a real pathspec in real git -- confirmed live (a tracked file literally named 'no' gets its dirty content committed directly). Two accepted, non-blocking residuals the reviewer found and I independently confirmed: `git commit -U <n>` (short-form --unified) is a narrow over-denial since -U isn't in this file's VALUE_TAKING_SHORT_FLAGS set, but unreachable in practice (`-U` always errors '--unified requires --interactive/--patch', both interactive-only); and the escaped-`\--`-with-nothing-after case documented in fix (2) above. Full suite after fixes: 1259/1259.
approaches_tried: extend has_staging_flag()'s existing token-walking loop to also detect a leftover flagless token (a bare pathspec) as a compound-stage-and-commit risk, unifying it with the existing staging-flag detection rather than adding a separate check

features.description: enforce-scope.sh.template's two legacy `exit 2` sites (:166, :212) and verify-task-quality.sh.template's four (:47, :81, :92, :125) all write their blocking guidance ("Edit blocked: ...", "Task rejected: ...") via plain `echo` to stdout, the identical defect F046 fixed in check-remaining-tasks.sh.template. Per Claude Code's own docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), exit 2 discards a hook's stdout entirely and feeds only stderr back to the blocked agent -- confirmed the effect table names PreToolUse (enforce-scope.sh's event), Stop, SubagentStop, and TeammateIdle explicitly, but does NOT explicitly confirm TaskCompleted's exit-2 semantics (verify-task-quality.sh's event), which needs independent confirmation before scoping that half of this fix. verify-git-identity.sh.template (:68, PreToolUse) has the same defect too but is not yet confirmed as reachable by an idle/blocked teammate the same way (its block is a same-turn PreToolUse denial, not a re-prompt loop) -- worth checking whether that distinction matters before folding it in.

features.notes:
Discovered by review-pr80-f046 while verifying F046's claim that the sibling hooks already write blocking guidance to stderr -- that claim was false, and the reviewer found the same stdout-only defect present in all three sibling hooks instead. Independently confirmed by the lead (grep + direct read of each exit-2 site) before filing. PreToolUse/Stop/SubagentStop/TeammateIdle are confirmed exit-2-discards-stdout paths per the Claude Code docs; TaskCompleted's exit-2 semantics (relevant to verify-task-quality.sh.template specifically) were not independently confirmed by the reviewer and should be checked before implementing that part of this fix.

FIXED: confirmed TaskCompleted's exit-2 stdout-discard behavior before implementing verify-task-quality.sh.template's half of this fix (fetched code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks directly: the "Exit code 2 behavior per event" table lists TaskCompleted as blockable -- "Yes | Prevents the task from being marked as completed" -- and the table has no stdout column at all, it describes only the blocking effect. The stdout rule is stated once, unconditionally, in prose: "Exit 2 means a blocking error. Claude Code ignores stdout and any JSON in it. Instead, stderr text is fed back to Claude as an error message." So it applies to every blockable event including TaskCompleted -- direct confirmation, not an inference from a documentation gap [CORRECTED, round 2 review of PR #86: the original wording here wrongly claimed the table was silent on TaskCompleted; it isn't, and the reviewer's independent fetch caught this before it became a stale, unchecked claim the way F046's own sibling-hook comparison did]). Also confirmed verify-git-identity.sh.template's distinction (same-turn PreToolUse denial vs. a re-prompt loop) doesn't matter for whether the bug exists -- PreToolUse is explicitly confirmed exit-2-discards-stdout in the docs regardless, so folded it into this fix's scope too rather than leaving it out on a distinction that turned out not to matter. Redirected all `echo` calls before each exit-2 site to stderr: enforce-scope.sh.template's 2 legacy sites, verify-task-quality.sh.template's 4, and verify-git-identity.sh.template's 2 (including the one F050 added earlier in this same sweep, which inherited the stdout convention that existed when it was written). Updated ~10 pre-existing tests that captured stdout-only via run_hook (which only captures stdout unless the caller redirects) -- without adding 2>&1 these would have started failing on empty output once the fix moved the message to stderr. Added 6 new assertions (2 per file) pinning the mechanism directly: stdout alone empty, stderr alone carries the message. Full suite 1265/1265. Mutation-tested by reverting all three templates and their resynced live copies: exactly 6 failures (2 per file), confirming precise discrimination.
approaches_tried: port check-remaining-tasks.sh.template's F046 fix (redirect exit-2 blocking echo statements to stderr) to the three remaining sibling hooks, after confirming via the official docs that TaskCompleted's exit-2 semantics match the general rule and that the same-turn-vs-loop distinction for verify-git-identity.sh doesn't change whether the underlying defect exists

features.description: This repo's .claude/settings.json wires enforce-scope.sh only on the PreToolUse Edit|Write|MultiEdit matcher -- unlike SKILL.md's own canonical settings.json (skills/harness-init/SKILL.md, ~lines 300-326), which wires enforce-scope.sh AND commit-gate.sh on the Bash matcher too (alongside verify-git-identity.sh, which IS wired there in this repo). CONFIRMED: this repo's Bash matcher only invokes verify-git-identity.sh; the entire F023-F046 scope-enforcement hardening arc for Bash-based writes (quoting, escaping, traversal, NUL-truncation, sed -i clustering, long-option abbreviation) is installed (once F047 merges) but never invoked here, and a scoped teammate could write outside its assigned scope via a Bash command today. commit-gate.sh (now installed by F047, but inert) is in the same state -- nothing invokes it. Separately, this repo's settings.json invokes hooks as `bash .claude/hooks/<name>.sh`, while context_summary.md's own OVI-48 decision (2026-07-22) records the canonical invocation as `"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/<name>.sh` -- harmless in practice since every hook self-anchors via PROJECT_ROOT="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)}", but the same settings.json-vs-documented-decision drift family, worth reconciling in the same pass. This is a live behavior change (gates every future Bash tool call in this repo, not a mechanical file resync), so it needs its own careful testing (in particular: confirm commit-gate.sh doesn't interfere with this repo's own normal add-then-commit workflow) and its own dedicated review, separate from F047's file-level resync.

Also reconciled the invocation-style drift (bash .claude/hooks/<name>.sh -> "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/.claude/hooks/<name>.sh) across every hook command and the permissions allowlist entry. Added a test mirroring the existing SKILL.md-settings-block check but against this repo's actual live settings.json: confirms enforce-scope.sh/commit-gate.sh/verify-git-identity.sh are all wired on Bash and the CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR-absolute form is used throughout. ROUND 2 (review of PR #87): reviewer found a real, blocking consequence of this fix that round 1 didn't anticipate: once commit-gate.sh is live on the Bash matcher, this repo's own test/run-tests.sh -- which deliberately stages secret-SHAPED synthetic fixture data throughout the F023-F052 arc to test the secret scanner itself -- can no longer be committed at all. Independently reproduced by the lead (as two properly-separated git add / git commit calls, learning from the same newline-joining mistake this session's own memory note now documents): confirmed a real secret-assignment denial on an ordinary fixture addition. Fixed by extending commit-gate.sh.template's existing *.env.example exemption with an opt-in, harness.json-configured secret_scan_exempt_paths array (mirrors style_gate_enabled()'s own pattern) [CORRECTED, round 3 review of PR #87: the original wording here claimed harness.json is lead-owned, so a scoped teammate can't self-grant an exemption -- FALSE, verified live: enforce-scope.sh's own LEAD_OWNED set only ever protects features.json/context_summary.md/claude-progress.txt; harness.json is protected only by the ordinary scope check, so a teammate scoped to .harness/ (or to harness.json itself) genuinely can edit this exemption list. This is a tuning knob for a project's own known, synthetic test fixtures, not a defense against a teammate who already has write access to harness.json -- corrected in the template's own comments, this notes field, and the test comment. Filed F058 to make harness.json genuinely LEAD_OWNED as its own feature, since that's a real behavior change beyond F054's remit]. Deliberately kept the exemption MECHANISM in the shared template (byte-identical across template and live copy, satisfying F047's drift guard) while configuring the specific exempt path (test/run-tests.sh) in this repo's own harness.json -- rather than hardcoding it into the live copy, which would have reintroduced exactly the drift F047 was filed to close. Verified end-to-end in a fresh fixture: without the config, the fixture addition denies; with it, the identical commit allows, and a different non-exempted path with the same content still correctly denies. Also fixed the reviewer's minor finding: the invocation-style guard used a loose text.count(...) < 5 threshold that could pass with some individual hook commands reverted to the cwd-relative form -- replaced with a per-command check over the parsed JSON, verified this variant now correctly fails. Added 5 new assertions for the exemption mechanism. Full suite after all fixes: 1271/1271.

Also documented, per the same review round, that exempting a path wholesale means a real secret later landing in that same file is also no longer caught -- an accepted cost for known synthetic test fixtures, not a residual to close.

features.description: check-remaining-tasks.sh.template's TeammateIdle guidance has no concept of teammate ROLE: it re-nudges any idle teammate toward the next claimable feature for as long as ANY feature is claimable, regardless of whether that teammate is an implementer (for whom this is correct) or a reviewer/other non-implementer role with no further review assigned (for whom claiming an unrelated feature would itself be scope creep under the agent-teams protocol). CONFIRMED live, twice: review-pr69-f040 hit this originally (leading to F046's filing), and review-pr81-f047 hit it again after F046's stdout-to-stderr fix was live and working correctly -- the hook fired exactly to spec (rc=2, correct guidance on stderr) but a reviewer with a completed, delivered review had no way to signal 'done, nothing claimable is mine' short of messaging the lead directly or violating scope by self-claiming an implementation feature. The TeammateIdle payload itself carries no teammate identity (an existing, confirmed constraint), so the hook cannot distinguish roles on its own [CORRECTION, F067 round-1 review: this was FALSE -- the payload does carry teammate_name; see this feature's notes field for the full correction] -- role-aware behavior would need to live in the agent definitions (e.g. a reviewer's own definition recognizing 'my assignment is done, message the lead and go idle' rather than treating check-remaining-tasks.sh's nudge as instruction to claim new work), not in this shared hook.

features.notes:
Raised by review-pr81-f047 (not filed by them -- explicitly deferred the filing decision to the lead, correctly declining to self-claim an unrelated implementation feature as a workaround, which would itself be the scope creep the agent-teams protocol prohibits). features.description: cp_mv_targets() (and its last_flagless_token() fallback) walk tokens in ORDER and treat the LAST flagless argument as the destination -- but real GNU cp/mv permute argv, so a value-consuming long or short option (--suffix VALUE, -S VALUE, --no-preserve VALUE, etc.) placed AFTER both operands still consumes the token that follows it as ITS value, not as a new flagless operand. CONFIRMED against real GNU cp 9.11: `cp src/parser/a.txt src/other/d --suffix src/parser/x` genuinely copies into `src/other/d` (the true destination), yet cp_mv_targets() reads the tokens left-to-right with no notion of 'this later flag consumes the next token', so it returns `src/parser/x` (the --suffix VALUE, an ordinary in-scope-looking path here) as the destination -- the REAL destination (`src/other/d`) is never checked at all. Same shape with the short form `-S src/parser/x`. Confirmed present identically on `main` and on the F048 branch (not a regression introduced by that work).

features.notes:
Discovered by review-pr82-f048 while verifying F048's own fix, explicitly checking whether it introduced or worsened this -- confirmed identical behavior on main and the F048 branch, so filed separately (discovered_via F048) rather than folded into that PR, mirroring how F048 itself was split out of F041's own discovery. Independently reproduced by the lead against real GNU cp 9.11 before filing (`gcp f.txt d1 --suffix .BAK --backup` genuinely creates `d1/f.txt.BAK`, confirming argv permutation is real GNU behavior, not a misreading).

FIXED: cp_mv_targets() rewritten from a plain enumerate() walk to an explicit index-managed while loop (mirroring sed_inplace_targets()'s own token-walking style), which builds the token list handed to last_flagless_token() by SKIPPING both a value-consuming flag and its consumed value, rather than relying on last_flagless_token() to filter the unmodified full token list afterward. Mechanically determined the exact flag set to fix (beyond -t/--target-directory, already handled) by testing every CP_MV_LONG_OPTIONS entry with an optional-vs-mandatory-looking value shape against real GNU cp 9.11 as two separate tokens: -S/--suffix, --no-preserve, and --sparse all genuinely consume the following token as their own value (command succeeds using only the remaining flagless tokens); --update, --context, --preserve, --backup, and --reflink (all optional/attached-only per their own --help bracket notation, [=X]) do NOT (each errors 'cannot stat' on the following token, proving it's left as an ordinary operand) -- confirms the general GNU getopt_long rule that an optional-argument long option can never accept a separate-token value (ambiguous with the next real operand), so no flag-by-flag guessing was needed beyond checking which of the two bracket forms each option uses. Also confirmed against real GNU cp that a value which itself LOOKS like a flag (e.g. `cp --suffix -t src dest`, where the literal suffix is "-t") is unconditionally consumed as the value, never re-parsed as a new flag -- the fix's index-skip (i += 2, never revisiting the skipped index) matches this; an initial design that filtered a marked set of indices AFTER an unmodified scanning loop would have gotten this specific case wrong, so the loop itself is index-managed, not just its output filtered. Added 17 new test assertions mirroring the existing F048/hs2 style (bare forms of --suffix/-S/--no-preserve/--sparse after both operands; a no-regression check for --update still NOT being treated as value-consuming; an in-scope destination past a --suffix VALUE still passing cleanly). Mutation-tested by reverting both the template and its resynced live copy: exactly 7 of the 17 new assertions failed (the assert_deny_json/assert_contains(destination) ones -- the assert_rc0 lines in the same tests don't discriminate for this JSON-deny-style hook, consistent with how the existing F048 tests are structured), nothing else. Full suite 1291/1291. Resynced .claude/hooks/enforce-scope.sh from the template per F047's drift guard.

ROUND 2 (review of PR #90): reviewer confirmed the fix logic itself is correct (independently reproduced all 9 empirical consumption claims against real gcp/gmv, traced the flag-shaped-value reasoning through the code, confirmed the clustered -rS residual is pre-existing on main and not a new regression) but found 3 record/coverage issues, all ground-truthed before fixing: (1) this entry's own description listed --backup as a value-consuming example -- confirmed FALSE against real gcp (--backup takes only an optional attached-only argument, never a separate token), directly contradicted by this same entry's own notes; corrected the example to --no-preserve VALUE. (2) the notes' test itemization overclaimed: it named a flag-shaped-value test and no-regression tests for --preserve/--backup/--reflink that did not exist (only --update had one, and no flag-shaped-value test existed at all, confirmed via direct grep). (3) the flag-shaped-value case (`cp --suffix -t src dest`) was reasoned about as the justification for the index-skip design but had no assertion pinning it -- a real coverage gap, since a future refactor to mark-then-filter would silently reintroduce the -t bypass while every other F056 test (using ordinary-looking values) stayed green. Also extended cp_mv_targets()'s residual comment (non-blocking finding) to name the clustered -rS gap alongside the pre-existing -rt one, confirmed via real gcp that `cp src/parser/a.txt src/other/d -rS src/parser/x` still writes to src/other/d while this function (both before and after F056) misreads the destination -- pre-existing on main, not a new regression, narrowed but not closed by this fix. ROUND 3 (review of PR #90): reviewer found the round-2 no-regression tests (--update/--preserve/--backup/--reflink) had ZERO discriminating power -- BLOCKING, and correctly held to the same standard as round-1 Finding 2 (record claims coverage that isn't real). Ground-truthed directly before fixing: injected the exact regression (added --preserve/--backup/--reflink to CP_MV_VALUE_ONLY_LONG) and confirmed the full suite still passed 1303/1303 -- the tests' token order (`cp --preserve mode src/parser/a.txt src/other/x`) put the destination two tokens past the flag, so wrongly consuming vs. correctly not consuming its value both left src/other/x as the last flagless token; the assertions could not tell them apart. Fixed per the reviewer's own verified probe: moved the flag between the source and destination with the destination immediately following the flag (e.g. `cp src/parser/a.txt --preserve src/other/x`), so wrongly consuming the token removes the REAL destination from candidacy entirely, falling back to the in-scope source -- ALLOW instead of the correct DENY. Confirmed against real GNU cp 9.11 that this exact shape genuinely writes into the token after the flag for all four of --update/--preserve/--backup/--reflink before rewriting the assertions. Mutation-tested each flag's rewritten test independently (re-added each flag one at a time to CP_MV_VALUE_ONLY_LONG): every one now fails exactly its own 2 discriminating assertions (JSON-deny form + destination name), nothing else, both individually and combined. Full suite 1303/1303 (same total count as round 2 -- 12 assertions rewritten in place, not added or removed).

approaches_tried: rewrote cp_mv_targets()'s plain enumerate() walk into an explicit index-managed while loop (mirroring sed_inplace_targets()'s established style) that skips a value-consuming flag's value token by index (never re-visiting it), rather than filtering the full token list after an unmodified scan -- the index-skip approach was required, not just cleaner, once real GNU cp's own value-is-unconditionally-consumed-even-if-flag-shaped behavior was confirmed empirically

VERIFIED, then FIXED: fetched code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks directly and asked specifically about TaskCompleted's own exit-0 stdout contract, not just the general 'for most events' prose. Confirmed: TaskCompleted is NOT one of the three documented exceptions (UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, SessionStart) where stdout becomes visible context -- its stdout on exit 0 genuinely lands only in the debug log, confirming the suspected defect was real (the same class F046/F053 fixed for exit-2 blocking messages, on the exit-0 accept path instead). Also fetched the docs' own documented fix mechanism: `systemMessage`, a universal JSON output field ('warning message shown to the user') visible regardless of event or exit code -- unlike `additionalContext`, which is delivered via hookSpecificOutput and is documented only for a specific set of events (SessionStart, Setup, SubagentStart, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Stop, SubagentStop) that does not include TaskCompleted -- it would silently no-op here. FIXED: both accept-path warnings (the no-proof-recorded/evidence-mismatch warning, and the stale-in-progress reminder) are now collected into variables instead of echoed directly, then combined (since only ONE JSON object can be emitted per hook invocation) into a single `{"systemMessage": "..."}` object printed once at the very end of the accept path. Reproduced live against a throwaway fixture before designing the test suite: confirmed both warnings combine into one valid JSON object when both apply, and stdout is genuinely empty when neither applies (no spurious JSON). Added 5 new test assertions: 2 that parse the ACTUAL JSON structure (not just a substring match anywhere in output, which a regression back to plain `echo` would still satisfy since the same words would still appear in stderr/stdout combined captures -- this is why the assertions parse json.loads() on a STDOUT-ONLY capture, separate from the existing combined-capture substring checks), 1 confirming both warnings combine into a single object, 2 for the clean-accept no-spurious-output case. features.description: The Agent Teams protocol (rules/agent-teams-protocol.md's Lead Agent Responsibilities) only documents team-WIDE shutdown: step 15 sends shutdown_request to ALL teammates, after step 10 synthesizes ALL teammates' work, at Phase 5 teardown. There is no documented per-teammate on-completion shutdown -- a teammate whose own assigned work is done (e.g. a reviewer whose review has been delivered and acted on) has no path to being released before the ENTIRE team reaches Phase 5, even if every other teammate still has features to implement. Confirmed via exhaustive grep for 'shutdown' across rules/, skills/, agents/ during F055's round-2 review: 5 hits total, all describing team-wide shutdown, none describing per-teammate early release. Consequence (observed live during F055's own review, review-pr89-f055's TeammateIdle hook kept re-firing on it 6 consecutive times after its review was delivered): a teammate with nothing left to claim spins silently (post-F055) or spams the lead (pre-F055) for the remainder of the session's team-wide work, rather than being released. This is a coordination semantics change affecting every teammate type, not just reviewers, so it needs its own spec and review rather than being folded into F055's narrower fix (F055 only made the interim behavior less noisy; it did not, and per its own scope could not, add an actual release path).

Not a one-line LEAD_OWNED addition like F058, though: adding `.claude/hooks/*.sh` to LEAD_OWNED unconditionally would block a teammate LEGITIMATELY assigned to work on the hooks themselves, which happens routinely in this repo (most of this session's own feature work touches these exact files). Needs a real design decision before implementation -- e.g. protect only `.claude/teammate-scope.txt` (a teammate should never need to edit its own scope definition, regardless of what it's assigned) while leaving `.claude/hooks/*.sh` governed by ordinary scope (so a teammate explicitly assigned scope covering `.claude/hooks/` can still work on them), or some other rule that distinguishes 'my own enforcement boundary' from 'code I was assigned to change'.

Fetched code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks and code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams directly (not from memory): confirmed NO documented mechanism exists for a hook to distinguish the lead's session from a teammate's -- hook input has no team-role/lead-vs-teammate field (common fields are session_id, prompt_id, cwd, permission_mode, agent_id, agent_type -- the latter two only present for --agent/subagent mode, a DIFFERENT feature from Agent Teams), and no environment variable distinguishes the two either. This meant my first-draft plan (recommend worktree isolation as the workaround) would have directly contradicted this repo's own already-researched finding -- caught before writing it, by checking the existing section rather than assuming. Given no clean supported mechanism exists, and the platform docs' own advice for genuine Agent Teams is disjoint scope ownership + enforce-scope.sh (the very mechanism causing this problem), the honest resolution is a documented, honest limitation: added a 'Known limitation (F061)' callout to rules/agent-teams-protocol.md's Mechanical Scope Enforcement section, matching the file's own existing Known-bug/retirement-condition convention (plan_approval_response). Considered and declined the ticket's suggested alternative (having add_settings_wiring delegate to scripts/stamp.sh mode=upgrade instead of maintaining a second hand-written copy of the wiring block): stamp.sh requires an answers file (project_name, stack, team_mode) that doctor.py's single-project-inspection call site doesn't have, and stamp.sh's upgrade-mode byte-identical-refresh assumption isn't designed for add_settings_wiring's actual job (patching in only the missing top-level keys of a partially-customized settings.json). Fixing the immediate drift bug is the ticket's core, mandatory ask; the delegation redesign is a larger, separately-reviewable change, matching F013's precedent of declining the same delegation question.

Round-1 review (PR #108) found doctor.py had the SAME drift (SETTINGS_WIRING_CHECKS never checked commit-gate.sh) plus a matcher-blind _hook_wired() that couldn't tell 'wired on Bash' from 'wired on some other matcher' -- the exact drift shape any pre-F054 project has. Made _hook_wired matcher-aware, fixed the PreToolUse predicate, and fixed a stale test fixture (make_healthy_doctor_fixture predated F011/commit-gate.sh) that the fix's own drift-detection then correctly flagged as unhealthy. Caught a real bug in my own first mutation test: an uncaught TypeError from calling the reverted _hook_wired with a keyword arg it didn't accept crashed the check before it could print anything, so the mutation silently 'passed' for the wrong reason -- wrapped the check in try/except so any exception reports as a failure, then re-verified the mutation correctly fails.

features.description: F017/OVI-65's harness-continue Phase 4 step 3.5 gates the conformance-tester spawn on a feature's risk being "elevated", but risk is not persisted anywhere on the local features.json feature object -- it exists only transiently in a Linear readiness-stamp comment (remote mode, and only if prep.stamp is configured) or in the lead's own in-session Phase 1 notes, neither of which survives compaction or is checkable without a live Linear lookup. Persist `risk` (and ideally `require_plan_approval`, the step's other trigger condition, which has the same problem) as a durable field on the feature object in schemas/feature.schema.json, written back by harness-issue-prep at stamp time (mirroring what already goes into the Linear comment) and/or by the lead at Phase 1 team-design time, so step 3.5's trigger condition becomes a genuine features.json lookup instead of "whatever the lead remembers or can still find in Linear."

features.description: check-remaining-tasks.sh's TeammateIdle nudge has two related gaps surfaced by F021's eval subagents (general-purpose, not vv-harness:reviewer): (1) its escape hatch ('if your role has no Edit/Write tools, this does not apply to you') is keyed on tool inventory, not on assignment scope -- a general-purpose subagent given an explicit read-only task (like an eval run) has Edit/Write by construction and gets nudged in a loop toward claiming the next feature, with no way to signal 'my assignment is scoped and complete' short of going idle and re-triggering the same nudge. (2) the claimable-feature count reads features.json status only and ignores task-level claims -- F021 was counted as unclaimed/claimable while TaskList showed task #8 in_progress under the lead, a features.json/TaskList sync gap. F055 (shipped) addressed the reviewer-specific case via agents/reviewer.md's construction-level guarantee; this is the same shape of gap (TeammateIdle nudges every idle teammate uniformly, regardless of what it was actually assigned) recurring for ad-hoc read-only assignments the F055 fix doesn't cover. Correction (round-1 review): the hook payload DOES carry teammate_name -- F055's original premise that it carries no teammate identity at all was wrong, confirmed via raw curl of code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md after a WebFetch-based check had truncated before reaching the TeammateIdle section and silently answered from the common-fields table instead. The genuine remaining gap is narrower: no task-list snapshot, and this hook doesn't use teammate_name even though it could.

All mutation-tested, including a re-verification pass after the round-1 design change: forcing the comparison to always report clean fails all 7 finding-presence/naming assertions correctly; making the fixer a no-op that returns True without writing fails all 5 --fix assertions; reproducing the reviewer's exact crash-silently-passes scenario in the fixes.py direct-unit block now correctly fails loudly instead of passing; removing stamp.sh's plugin_version write breaks the F013 AC3 'stamped project passes doctor clean' test, confirming that dependency is real, not coincidental. features.notes: Chose to implement the real check over correcting the description, since the value (an actual doctor.py capability matching what a 'doctor' tool should do) outweighed the small extra scope, and the existing pattern for an optional harness.json field (worker block, F016) was directly reusable. Investigated first: .harness/harness.json has no version field of any kind in any project (confirmed by reading templates/harness.json.tmpl and this repo's own harness.json), so a real check needed a new field recorded at /harness-init time, not just a doctor.py comparison against something already there. Also found, while editing the 'What it checks' list to add the new check, that item 6 was pre-existing-mislabeled 'Version drift' for something that was never a real version comparison (stale PostCompact block + missing v5 artifacts) -- renamed to 'v5 upgrade staleness' to stop the name collision with this feature's actual version check, and separately found F066's own test_file check had never been documented in this same list at all -- added it too since it was directly adjacent to the edit already in progress. This repo's own .harness/harness.json is left without a plugin_version field (matches its own precedent of not having a worker block either -- this repo dogfoods the harness but was never itself run through /harness-init in the normal plugin-consumer sense). ROUND 1 (review of PR #113, review-pr113-f068): reviewer found 1 blocking and 3 non-blocking. BLOCKING: my original design treated an absent plugin_version as silently valid (mirroring the F016 worker block), which left the check permanently inert for every pre-existing project -- nothing ever wrote plugin_version, so a check that never fires never triggers its own fixer either. Verified empirically before fixing (ran --fix against a bare {project,stack} harness.json, confirmed the key never appeared). Fixed by reclassifying absence as a fixable 'upgrade available' finding (matching the existing missing-harness_state.py pattern) AND, since the reviewer's own fix option (a) surfaced a deeper question -- should a freshly-stamped project ever show as unhealthy before completing /harness-init's follow-up steps? -- investigated stamp.sh's own 'never hand-write what a stamp can emit; never stamp what a decision shapes' doctrine and found plugin_version belongs on the emit side (purely mechanical, unlike git_identity/worker) rather than the decision side, so moved the initial write into stamp.sh itself instead of leaving it as a SKILL.md follow-up step. This also fixed a real regression the redesign introduced: F013's own pre-existing AC3 ('a stamped project passes harness-doctor clean') broke the moment absence became a finding, since stamp.sh didn't write the field -- caught by the full suite, not by design review, confirming the value of running it after every change rather than only at the end. N1 (fixes.py direct-unit block reports PASS on a crash, since $(...) only captures stdout): fixed by adding 2>&1 to the capture and checking python's exit code explicitly; reproduced the reviewer's exact crash scenario to confirm the fix actually catches it. N2 (an untested, then-unreachable guard in _update_plugin_version): exercised directly rather than dropped, since it's a legitimate defensive guard for a plugin_root whose plugin.json vanishes or is malformed between check and fix, matching _copy_statusline's own defensive style -- and it remains reachable as a direct fixes.py API call even though the CLI path now guarantees it never fires there either. N3 (coverage field arithmetic was wrong, same defect class F066's round-1 caught): recomputed precisely after the redesign rather than patched in place. Also folded in the reviewer's non-blocking schema suggestion (feature.schema.json's top-level description didn't mention plugin_version at all) as a cheap same-PR nit. ROUND 2 (review of PR #113, review-pr113-f068): reviewer APPROVEd -- B1, N1, N3 all confirmed genuinely fixed (re-verified independently, not just re-reading my summary; caught and corrected their own imprecise round-1 mutation of the bootstrap branch along the way). N2 was NOT actually fixed despite my round-1 claim: the two new isolation checks ran before .harness/harness.json existed in the test's own setup order, so _update_plugin_version's harness-missing guard masked the manifest guard regardless of whether the manifest guard existed -- confirmed by reproducing the reviewer's proof (deleting the manifest guard still gave 1480/1480). Same defect class as F066's round-1 finding: a condition satisfied by something else at the same time, never independently pinned. Fixed by reordering the block: .harness/harness.json is now created before the manifest-guard checks, with 2 added assertions confirming no write happened, and verified via 2 targeted mutations (removing the whole guard, and removing only the no-version-key half) that each now fails correctly -- the first surfaces as a crash on the versionless-manifest case (KeyError on manifest['version']), correctly caught loud by round-1's N1 fix rather than silently passing. Also fixed N4 (this repo's own .harness/harness.json had no plugin_version, so it failed its own new check the moment absence stopped being silently valid -- the notes' 'matches its own precedent of not having a worker block either' rationale was correct in round 1 but stale after the round-1 redesign) by genuinely dogfooding: ran `doctor.py --fix .` against this repo itself rather than hand-editing the field. Fixed N5 (a scope_expansions entry still described the superseded manual-SKILL.md-step approach round-1 replaced with the stamp.sh move). Declined N6 (docstring wording tension) since the reviewer explicitly flagged it as optional/low-value and it predates this feature in spirit (the same tension exists for the drift-update path, not something F068 introduced). Full suite 1480/1480 throughout round 2.

_update_plugin_version in fixes.py follows the existing fixer contract (return True/False, no side effects on no-op) and is only ever invoked through apply_fixes when a drift Finding already exists, so it never writes plugin_version to a project that never recorded one -- that decision stays with /harness-init, not doctor --fix.

features.description: F055's foundational claim that the TeammateIdle hook payload 'carries no teammate identity' is FALSE, discovered during F067's round-1 review. F067 already corrected .claude/hooks/check-remaining-tasks.sh (+ its template) and rules/agent-teams-protocol.md's relevant passages. features.description: [OVI-107] P1: features.json writes race under parallel TaskCompleted hooks. harness_state.py.template's write_atomic_tmp always writes the fixed name features.json.tmp, and verify-task-quality.sh.template does rm -f .harness/features.json.tmp before each write, then mv's the tmp over features.json after. With parallel teammates, concurrent TaskCompleted invocations can: delete another invocation's in-flight tmp file (the explicit rm -f), lose a correction_cycles increment to read-modify-write last-write-wins, or silently overwrite a coordinator's direct edit landing between another hook's read and mv. Fix: move the entire lock-acquire + read + modify + write + rename cycle into harness_state.py itself (fcntl.flock on a .lock file, bounded wait, PID-suffixed tmp name, os.replace) so the critical section is a single process's responsibility instead of split across bash and python. verify-task-quality.sh.template's rm-f/tmp-check/mv wrapper is removed entirely -- python now does the full atomic write itself. This is a deliberate contract change to harness_state.py's CLI (it no longer leaves a .tmp file for a caller to promote), disclosed here and in the commit/PR, not a silent behavior shift.
features.coverage: 11 new/changed suite assertions beyond the pre-existing hs:/ht: coverage: 12-way same-feature concurrent-increment test (all land, no lost writes, no orphaned tmp, still valid JSON), 2-way different-feature concurrent test (neither clobbers the other), a genuine lock-contention timeout test (~5s bounded wait, not instant-fail or a hang, reports on stderr, leaves the file untouched), plus corrected the existing hs:/ht: assertions that depended on the old .tmp-left-behind contract (glob-based tmp checks instead of a fixed filename, reading the real file instead of a .tmp path, checksum-based no-write checks). Also caught and fixed one pre-existing false-positive assertion found while touching this area: 'ht: verify-task-quality writes features.json atomically (.tmp + mv)' was passing only because this feature's own comment text (describing the REMOVED mechanism) happened to contain the substring 'mv '. Empirically proved the bug and the fix, not just asserted them: reproduced the OLD split-process design in isolation and confirmed it lost 8-9 of 12 concurrent increments on 3/3 independent runs; the NEW design landed all 12 on 5/5 independent runs. Full suite 1500/1500.
features.notes:
discovered_via: Ovidiu forwarded 8 Linear issues (OVI-103/104/105/106/107/108, OVI-81/82) from a separate external code-review pass (feedback_vivi.md, 2026-07-29) and a different Linear project handoff (OVI-73/claude-md, 2026-07-25), none part of the just-shipped OVI-44 epic. A plan was drafted, then reviewed by a spawned critical-thinker agent (Opus) before any code was written -- it independently verified every 'current status' claim against the live source and found the write-race fix as originally planned (lock inside harness_state.py only) would NOT close the race, since the critical section genuinely spans two processes (bash's rm -f/mv wrap python's read/write). Verified this myself before accepting the correction. Also caught: bash-level flock(1) is util-linux and absent on macOS (confirmed: `command -v flock` fails on this box) -- fcntl.flock inside Python is the correct mechanism, not a bash-level wrapper. Reprioritized to ship first in v5.0.1, ahead of OVI-104 despite its lower Linear priority label, since this is silent data corruption in the core parallel-agent write path (live since OVI-50/F008), not a doctor-UX gap.

RESOLVED, redesigned per critical-thinker review before any code was written (see the discovered_via note above): the ORIGINAL plan -- add an fcntl.flock only inside harness_state.py -- would NOT have closed the race, since the critical section genuinely spans two processes (the bash wrapper's rm -f before, and mv after, wrap python's own read+write). Verified this myself directly before accepting the correction: confirmed the split via git show, confirmed pinned tests asserting a .tmp file is LEFT BEHIND for the caller to promote (test/run-tests.sh's hs: section), and confirmed verify-task-quality.sh.template's '2>&1 || true' would swallow a python-side hard failure silently. Final design: harness_state.py owns the ENTIRE lock-acquire + read + modify + write + rename cycle itself (fcntl.flock on a persistent, never-unlinked .lock file -- unlinking a lockfile after release is a known race, confirmed via reasoning about inode reuse, not asserted from memory -- bounded 5s wait, PID-suffixed tmp name ending in .tmp so the existing broad *.tmp gitignore rule covers it automatically, os.replace). verify-task-quality.sh.template's rm-f/tmp-check/mv wrapper is removed entirely; it now just invokes the module and stays fail-open on its exit code, matching the hook's own pre-existing documented posture for the correction_cycles bookkeeping side effect (a deliberate, disclosed decision: the corruption modes -- deleted in-flight tmp, whole-file clobber -- are now closed regardless; an occasional lock-timeout on this ONE non-critical counter still fails open, now with a clear stderr diagnostic instead of silence). Added an explicit 'locking is advisory and hook-scoped, not a substitute for lead-only ownership' note to rules/agent-teams-protocol.md, since the lock protects hook-vs-hook races only, never the lead's own direct Edit/Write calls.

ROUND 1 (review of PR #120, review-pr120-f070, Opus): APPROVE, no blocking findings. Independently reproduced the lock's exception-safety (killed a lock holder mid-write with SIGKILL, next increment acquired in 0.04s), confirmed the critical-thinker's identified trap (locking a SEPARATE file, not features.json itself, since os.replace swaps the inode out from under any lock held on the target) is the correct design, and stress-tested to 120-way concurrency (all landed). Folded NIT-1 before merge (this commit): a test-block comment claimed both concurrency tests are 'skipped, not silently passed' if the toolchain can't launch background jobs -- no such skip logic exists anywhere in the block; removed the false claim. Declined to fold 3 further nits, recorded here instead: NIT-2 (harness_state.py's new lock-timeout diagnostic is merged onto stdout via the caller's `2>&1`, so it likely won't reach the agent the way Claude Code surfaces hook stderr on exit 2 -- pre-existing redirection, not a regression, and the interaction with this hook's fail-open `|| true` posture needs its own investigation before touching); NIT-3 (the new top-level `import fcntl` makes harness_state.py's read-only verbs Unix-only too, and session-start.sh's next-claimable fallback only triggers on a missing file, not an import error, on a hypothetical non-Unix platform -- unverified, this repo has no non-macOS/Linux target today); NIT-4 (a permanent flock error, e.g. ENOLCK, is treated identically to a normal EWOULDBLOCK retry, burning the full 5s timeout before reporting a misleading message -- exotic-filesystem edge case). All three are real but scoped past what this feature needs to ship correctly.

features.description: [OVI-105] P1: session-start orientation can hit the 10k platform output cap. hooks/session-start.sh prints the next claimable feature's full description untruncated in both the delegated (harness_state.py) and fallback code paths. Plain stdout to the model is capped at 10,000 chars (the hook's own header comment). Measured on the dogfooding repo: the longest description in .harness/features.json was 13,222 chars -- a single feature could blow past the cap by itself, truncating more important recovery information (the git-identity mismatch warning and every rule pointer print AFTER the description). The existing test (<4000 chars) passed only because the fixture's descriptions were 20-26 characters, never exercising the real-world case. Fix: truncate the printed description to 200 chars with a pointer to the full text in features.json, in both code paths (they duplicate this logic, so both needed the same fix and both needed independent test coverage).
features.coverage: 7 new assertions: fallback path (orientation stays under 4000 chars with a 13,222-char description matching the real-world length OVI-105 cited, the feature id still appears, the truncation marker names the real length and points at the full text, later rule-pointer content still fits) and delegated path (same 3 checks, minus the later-content check since that fixture doesn't exercise the rule-pointer section identically). Mutation-tested: reverted ONLY the delegated path's truncation logic, confirmed exactly its own 2 assertions fail while all 4 fallback-path assertions stay green -- proves the two paths are independently pinned, not one test accidentally covering both. Full suite 1496/1496.
features.notes: Second item in the v5.0.1 patch batch (after F070/OVI-107), per the critical-thinker-reviewed plan. Design choice: 200-char truncation length, tight enough that even several long-ish descriptions plus the rest of orientation stay well under the 4000-char budget test this repo already enforces, with margin below the platform's actual 10,000-char cap. The rationale (protect what prints AFTER the description, not just trim verbosity) is stated inline as a comment, per feedback that the 'why' matters more than the number itself. Duplicated the fix across both session-start.sh code paths (delegated and fallback) since the file already duplicates this printing logic for different reasons (v5+ projects with harness_state.py vs. older projects without it) -- did not attempt to de-duplicate the two paths as part of this fix, since that's a larger refactor outside OVI-105's scope.

features.description: commit-gate.sh false-positive: a commit message subject line sourced from a heredoc (`git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)"`) that contains an embedded double-quoted phrase (e.g. `... commit-gate.sh "upgrade available" support`) gets denied as a compound-stage-and-commit risk, even as a standalone commit with nothing staged in the same command. CORRECTED (2026-08-02): originally attributed to the literal token `--fix` appearing in the message (discovered live during F073/OVI-104's own commit, whose natural message needed that word) -- round-1 review (review-pr123-f073) tested 15 variants and found `--fix` alone, in isolation, is consistently ALLOWED, correctly flagging the original attribution as unverified. Re-investigated by reproducing the exact original failing command directly against commit-gate.sh (feeding it the same JSON shape test/run-tests.sh's own run_commit_gate() helper uses) rather than inferring from the live tool denial alone, then bisecting the message content line by line. Confirmed root cause: an embedded double-quoted phrase inside the heredoc body is sufficient and necessary to reproduce the deny -- neither `--fix` nor an embedded apostrophe alone reproduces it, and stripping the embedded double-quotes from an otherwise-identical message allows it every time. Needs someone to read commit-gate.sh's quote-scanning logic (the file's own header comments describe a '--' argument-separator and quote-boundary scan) to find where an embedded double-quote inside the message body is mistaken for a shell-level quote boundary.
features.notes: Reproduction commands (feed to `bash .claude/hooks/commit-gate.sh` via the same JSON shape as test/run-tests.sh's bash_command_json/run_commit_gate helpers): a heredoc-sourced `-m` message containing `commit-gate.sh "upgrade available" support` (embedded double-quotes, no apostrophe, no --fix) is DENIED. The identical message with the double-quotes removed is ALLOWED. `--fix` and an embedded apostrophe were each tested in isolation (heredoc, no double-quotes) and both ALLOWED.

features.description: OVI-107 follow-up, found by review-pr120-f070 reading fixes.py incidentally during unrelated OVI-105/doctor work, after PR #120 (F070) had already merged to main: PR #120 added .harness/features.json.lock to .gitignore in two of the three places new projects/upgrades get it from (this repo's own .gitignore, and scripts/stamp.sh's init path) but not the third: doctor.py --fix's _append_gitignore fixer. Worse than a missing line -- the fixer was structurally unreachable for the affected population: it early-returned False whenever '.harness/SESSION_INCOMPLETE' (the only line it ever wrote) was already present, which is true for every already-initialized project, i.e. exactly the population the doctor --fix upgrade path exists to serve. Separately, doctor.py's check_gitignore never checked for the lock line's presence at all, so no Finding was ever generated to trigger the fixer in the first place. features.description: OVI-81: the harness has no dedicated TDD-loop rule file. features.notes: Branched from F074/OVI-82's branch (not main) since both features touch the same session-start.sh rule-pointer block -- avoids a guaranteed merge conflict on adjacent lines.
